# Lessons

## 2026-11-19 — SUCCESS PATTERN: fleet-build two anatomy-kit factory modules (research agents → builder agents), `docs/aircraft_assembly`, `docs/cammer_lense_factory`

**Goal:** two bilingual isometric factory models (737 final assembly ending in take-off; LG Innotek-style camera module ending in a phone) from scratch, with deep research.
**Pattern that worked:**
- 4 `research` agents in parallel (2 per topic: supply/structure vs. line/test; company/sites vs. process/competitors). They cannot write files: they return the report inline, and the lead saves it (`sed -n '5,$p'` of the saved tool output) to `<module>/research/`. Each report ends with a KEY NUMBERS TABLE and a CORRECTIONS list; builders were told to trust CORRECTIONS over the brief. It caught real errors (737 fuselage sections are joined in Wichita not Renton; 3 Renton lines not 2; first flights take off from Renton RNT 1,640 m then land at Boeing Field; 8.6 psi unverified; clean-room class 10 not ISO 6-7).
- 2 `senior-fullstack-coder` builders in parallel, one shared `BRIEF_COMMON.md` (session `files/`) + per-module prompt. Each copied `docs/auto-factory`'s architecture (pure `model.js`, `data.js`, `live.js` with a `window.__x` test hook, build.mjs with CSP hash, functional.py). ~2.3 h each; one builder wrote 500 tool calls of geometry before producing any HTML, so demand a full build within the first hour (a nudge via `write_agent` fixed it).
- Gates that were actually run: `node build.mjs --audit`, `lines.mjs` (camera first run: 717 of 1148 line ends floating, fixed by ending rollers/slats/seams on strokes), `tests/functional.py` (flaky timing on loaded software GL: poll real frames, never sleep).
- Do not commit another session's half-done edits: `docs/index.html` was being edited concurrently by another session; check `git log`/`git diff HEAD` right before staging so only your own hunks go in.
Full story: `docs/aircraft_assembly/README.md`, `docs/cammer_lense_factory/README.md`.

## 2026-11-19 — FAILURE ROUTE + SUCCESS PATTERN: bonupai v2.1 still "repair → unsuccessful" in PowerPoint; differential census found `ellipse` + `<a:gd name="adj">` (`pptx-tools/`, `bonupai/deck/dg.js`)

**Symptom:** `Bonupai_Tech_Guide_KO_v2.1.pptx` (and v1/v2) show the repair prompt and the repair fails; ~30 other pptxgenjs decks open fine. Zip, XML, XSD (`validate.py`), `pptx_audit.py`, Open XML SDK, LibreOffice and python-pptx were all green, so the QA process could not see it.
**Failure route:** v2.1's notesMaster/notes-size changes were a guess from gitbrent/PptxGenJS#1443; every other pptxgenjs deck (notes included) opens, and v1/v2/v2.1 fail alike, so the notesMaster was never the discriminator. Also ruled out with evidence: PNG/JPG integrity (all 256x256 RGBA, CRC/zlib ok), control/format/PUA characters, table grids, numeric ranges, rels/content types, zip header flags, scale (162 slides < 199 in a healthy deck), blob corruption in git.
**What found it (pattern):** stop validating the one deck in isolation and diff it against *all healthy decks from the same pipeline*: census of (element, attribute-names, child-order) signatures and of (preset, guide-name) pairs. Only one thing exists in bonupai and nowhere else: 176 `<a:prstGeom prst="ellipse"><a:avLst><a:gd name="adj"/>` shapes, because `dg.js` passed `rectRadius` to the one-digit `ellipse` badges and pptxgenjs writes `adj` for any `rectRadius`. XSD and the Open XML SDK accept any guide name, but ellipse/rect/line/diamond define none (a guide a preset does not define is reported as a corrupt/unopenable file in other tools' issue trackers, e.g. iOfficeAI/OfficeCLI#235, storytold/deckcraft#214).
**Fix:** `dg.js` passes `rectRadius` only to `roundRect`; `pptx_sanitize.py` drops guides from presets that define none (idempotent; run on the old v2.1 it removed exactly the 176); `pptx_audit.py` has a new `preset-guide` category (flags only bonupai across the repo before the fix); `bonupai/deck/build.js` now runs `pptx_audit.py` after the sanitizer and fails the build on any issue. v2.1 was rebuilt: the only slide-XML diff is the removed guides.
**Limits:** no PowerPoint here, so this is the best-evidence root cause, not a proven one (one report says PowerPoint ignores extra guides). If it still prompts, get the exact dialog text, Office build, Mac/Windows/Web, and bisect by building section subsets (`node build.js --only a,b1`) to find the failing slide range.

## 2026-11-18 — FAILURE ROUTE + SUCCESS PATTERN: fleet-translate an existing PPTX by editing unpacked XML; never keep fleet work in /tmp

**Symptom:** A system reboot wiped `/tmp` mid-run, destroying the unpacked deck, four agents' translations and the QA renders; everything had to be redone.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:**
- Keep the work dir (unpacked XML, renders, briefs) in the session `files/` folder, not `/tmp`; track agents in the `todos` table.
- Translating an existing deck: `unpack.py` → 4 agents, each owning a slide range (`slideN.xml` + `notesSlideN.xml`, edit only `<a:t>` and `lang`) with a shared glossary `BRIEF.md` → `pack.py --original` → LibreOffice render of both EN and KO → 3 rubber-duck QA agents (text, visual 1–14, visual 15–27) → apply fixes → repack and re-render changed slides.
- Set the theme `<a:ea typeface="">` to `Malgun Gothic` so Korean has an East-Asian font.
- QA findings that recur: cross-chunk term drift (베이스라인 vs 기준선, 약정 over-used for "commit"), a big-number shape followed by a sentence needing a joining particle ("60%+" + "의 기업이"; do not duplicate the number), a title run followed by a subtitle run in one paragraph needs an `<a:br>`. Text inside embedded pictures cannot be translated; report it instead.
Full story: `L200_FinOps_for_AI_Azure_and_GitHub_KO_v1.pptx` (source `L200 FinOps for AI Azure and GitHub.PPTX`, left unmodified).

## 2026-11-18 — FAILURE ROUTE: audio-energy checks passed but "chalk" was loud looping noise

**Symptom:** A user found the lesson's chalk sound too loud and unlike writing characters, despite passing playback/mute tests.
**Root cause:** A 1.5-second procedural noise loop at master gain `0.7` followed whole animation segments, including spaces. Tests checked only nonzero output and pause/mute silence, not source authenticity, loudness relative to narration, or pen lifts.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Embed licensed real chalk recordings (digitale.de / Freesound 178433, CC0), share per-character/stroke contact state with the renderer, leave spaces silent, and provide quiet default volume plus its own slider. The six-second voice-off fixture changed from -23.6 to -49.4 dBFS RMS; recorded contact starts increased from 2 to 18, with 36 silent space samples. Automated checks still do not establish subjective realism: listen before making that claim.
Full story: `chalk-talks/linear-function/verify_chalk.py`, `chalk-talks/linear-function/assets/chalk-writing-source.json`; global skill guidance: `~/.agents/skills/chalk-talk/docs/NARRATED_LESSONS.md` (repository paths in that document are scoped to this repo).

## 2026-11-18 — SUCCESS PATTERN: verify an offline narrated HTML lesson with real audio signals and complete playback

**Symptom:** A self-contained Korean chalkboard lesson needs both animated writing sounds and Foundry narration; a working mute button or advancing progress bar does not prove either sound exists.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Generate per-chapter MAI-Voice-2 MP3s through the existing Foundry AIServices account using Azure CLI Entra auth; embed clips and the Korean font in the delivered HTML. Test the actual `file://` artifact in offline Chrome. Decode every clip, measure Web Audio output through an analyser (nonzero while drawing, silent before play/on pause/on mute), exercise media-error notices, and play all chapters through the final stopped state. Inspect completed board screenshots separately from in-progress animation frames.
Full story: `chalk-talks/linear-function/README.md`, `verify_browser.py`, `verify_media.py`.

## 2026-11-17 — SUCCESS PATTERN: operational-readiness ladder (S0..S9) for a small ECS/RDS startup → price each step free-first vs managed, validate CLI/code offline

**Symptom / goal:** "how to raise 운영 준비 상태 step by step, with AWS uplift, complexity and CLI" + minimum observability + a 100-concurrent load test that never touches the real third-party site.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:**
- Order by risk removed per effort: fixed-reply ALB health check → `/readyz` (S0) → CloudWatch Logs JSON (S1) → alarms + SNS→Lambda→messenger (S2) → budgets (S8) → Sentry, EMF metrics, runbooks, load test → SLO/canary → tracing last. Free-first S0–S8 ≈ $8.9/mo vs managed ≈ $173/mo (AWS $118 + SaaS $55).
- ALB fails open and deregistered targets are invisible to `UnHealthyHostCount` → alarm `HealthyHostCount < 1`; DB checks belong in `/readyz/deep` for a canary, not in the ALB path. A GitHub Actions 5-minute cron is not free; Lambda + EventBridge ≈ $0.
- Load test: WireMock channel mock + FastAPI LLM stub + k6 in the QA landscape with no NAT/IGW; ≈ $59 per 3-hour 100-concurrent day. Offline CLI check: fake creds + `--endpoint-url http://127.0.0.1:9`.
- `cost_model.py` BOMs are gross unless `free_monthly` is set (free tier is account-wide); re-add every cost-table row by hand (an S6 row had `3.00 × 약 1 = ≈1`).
Full story: `bonupai/research/R-D.md`, `R-D_b.md`~`R-D_e.md`, `lessons/D.md`.

## 2026-11-17 — SUCCESS PATTERN: BCDR tier ladder for a single-EC2 startup → price T0..T6 cumulatively with a runnable cost model, verify every runbook command against the CLI reference

**Symptom / goal:** "BCDR for production + monthly cost per tier" for a Seoul (ap-northeast-2) ECS/RDS PostgreSQL+pgvector stack; needed AZ-failure survival, backup, and a DR region with CLI runbooks that are not hallucinated.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:**
- DR region must be **Tokyo**: RDS automated-backup replication Seoul→Osaka is unsupported. Backup-account copies need a CMK (not `aws/rds`); Logically-air-gapped vault can't copy RDS cross-Region; the RDS free backup allotment is per Region and needs a DB instance there (Tokyo replica → first 100 GB free).
- FIS "AZ Power Interruption" scenario excludes Fargate → custom template `aws:network:disrupt-connectivity` (`scope`, `duration=PT10M`) + stop-condition alarm (~$2–3/run at $0.10/action-min). ARC zonal shift `--away-from` wants an **AZ ID** (`apne2-az1`), `--comment` is required — read the CLI reference "Options" text rather than trusting memory.
- Cost (DB 100 GB, S3 200 GB, 5 %/day, FX 1,335): T1 +$57, T3 +$105 (T1+T3 $162), T4 +$202 (cum. $363), T5 +$319 (cum. $682), T6 ≥$2,400. Sensitivity on daily change rate (1→10 %) moves T1/T3 3×; always-on T4/T5 barely move. Cross-check the BOM JSONs with a rough price script (within ~1 %).
Full story: `bonupai/research/R-C.md`, `R-C_b.md`, `lessons/C.md`, `bom/C_T*.json`.

## 2026-11-17 — SUCCESS PATTERN: as-is "best guess" analysis of a single-EC2 + RDS stack → verify each guess against AWS docs, then quantify with a runnable capacity model

**Symptom / goal:** a customer's 12 guesses (A-01..A-12) about their own stack (t3.xlarge, ALB fixed health check, WAF Count, DB-as-queue) had to be confirmed/refuted for a deck without overclaiming.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:**
- T3 defaults to `unlimited` (surplus-credit charge, not throttle) — the real ceiling is 4 vCPU; ALB fails open on one target; EC2 auto-recovery only reacts to *system* status checks; Fargate lacks `sharedMemorySize` (Chromium `/dev/shm`). Mark each as verified vs `[검증 필요]`.
- Quantify with `bonupai/research/capacity_model.py` (Little's law, headroom, Poisson P99, per-family cost from the AWS Price List) and expose the dominant unknown (vCPU per job) as a sensitivity table.
- Keep per-file size ≤40KB by splitting early (`R-A.md`/`R-A_b.md`); a Python rewrite script is not a substitute for the edit tool.
Full story: `bonupai/research/R-A.md`, `R-A_b.md`, `lessons/A.md`.

## 2026-11-16 — SUCCESS PATTERN: 64-slide Korean Spec Kit deck from the real CLI, 8 authors → generate images → tune labels on contact sheets → 4 QA agents → 10 fix agents

**Symptom / goal:** one comprehensive Korean guide to GitHub Spec Kit (`spec-kit/`, `Spec_Kit_Guide_KO_v1.pptx`) with command-level demos that must match what `specify` actually does.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:**
- Facts first: `uv tool install` the real `specify` CLI in `/tmp`, run `--help` for every subcommand, `init` into a scratch dir and keep the raw output next to a `FACTS.md`. Authors may only use FACTS.md. Authors still flagged where the docs describe upstream `main` rather than the installed version; keep those as `[추정]`/`[검증 필요]` in the speaker notes only, never on the slide.
- Order: scaffold (`lib.js`, `build.js`, `make_placeholders.py`) → 8 parallel authors (own `sections/X.js`, `prompts/X.json`, `labels/X.json`) → ONE sequential `gen_images.py` run → `contact.py` (panel + current pills + 10 % grid) label tuning by one agent per section group → full build → 4 read-only visual-QA agents → 10 fix agents (one per section, same ownership rules) → rebuild → second QA pass.
- Visual QA kept finding the same classes: stacked blocks with 0.05–0.15in gaps, code blocks with dead space at the bottom, pills over icons, picture/label mismatches (box counts differ from the table). Give every fix agent a numbered `FIX_BRIEF.md` (gap ≥ 0.18in, code block height = `lines*0.2+0.3`, one allowed image regeneration) instead of ad-hoc instructions.
- Fresh-eyes QA found a real lib bug: pptxgenjs `margin` arrays are POINTS in `[left, right, bottom, top]` order. `code()` passed inches, so every code block had ~0 padding. Fix it once in `lib.js`.
- Failure routes: (1) `qa_check.py` counted `ImgLabelLeader` connector lines as labels → fake "label font < 9pt" errors; skip them. (2) A wait loop using `pgrep -f "<cmd>"` inside `bash -c "<cmd>"` matches itself and never ends; wait on the PID with `kill -0`. (3) `gen_images.py` loads prompts once at start, so prompts added later need a second run. (4) Some agents wrote files via bash heredoc/Python despite the edit-tool rule; content was fine, but say it explicitly in the brief. (5) FACTS went stale in three places (BMAD agent count, the bundled `speckit` workflow has only 2 gates, 4 not 3 persistence models): when an author contradicts FACTS with a cited doc, trust the doc and record it in the notes.
- `git status` showed only `?? spec-kit/`; per the existing rule the user runs `gitall.sh`, so nothing was committed.
Full story: `spec-kit/README.md`, `spec-kit/deck/`.

## 2026-11-10 — FAILURE ROUTE: `START_N=N node build.js --only <id>` numbers the first slide N+1

**Symptom:** QA asked for `START_N=22` to get deck slides 22–23, but the footer page numbers rendered 23–24 (`state.n` is incremented before the slide is created).
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Use `START_N=<first slide number − 1>` (here 21) and confirm against `out/full_text.md` (`<!-- Slide number: 22 -->`). Notes cross-references must use deck numbers (guardrail baseline = slide 22), never section-local ones.
Full story: `lgu-easm-rollout/deck/sections/safe.js`.

## 2026-11-10 — SUCCESS PATTERN: inventory "all Foundry-related Azure Policy" from the Azure/azure-policy repo first, then reconcile with Learn

**Symptom:** The Learn policy reference (`ai-services/policy-reference`) lags the repo and mixes classic hub, Search and Cognitive Services; the CMK policy looks like it covers Foundry but does not; model-router preview policies named on Learn do not exist in the repo.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** `gh api repos/Azure/azure-policy/contents/built-in-policies/policyDefinitions/{Cognitive Services,Azure Ai Services,Monitoring,Search,Machine Learning}` + `policySetDefinitions/Cognitive Services`, parse each JSON (displayName, `parameters.effect.allowedValues/defaultValue`, `metadata.deprecated/preview`, mode) instead of scraping docs. Findings (HEAD f096d8de, release 3.2026.1009.2): 30 account-level definitions (4 deprecated → 26 active) + 1 guardrail initiative; the CMK policy's `excludedKinds` default contains AIServices/CognitiveServices, so it never evaluates Foundry accounts unless overridden; content-filter, approved-model, eligibility and tool policies use mode `Microsoft.CognitiveServices.Data` and the content-filter ones are Audit/Disabled only; `Machine Learning/` policies are hub (classic) only; capability host / connection / project managed-network have no built-in policy → Microsoft ships 4 custom samples in `microsoft-foundry/foundry-samples/infrastructure/infrastructure-setup-bicep/05-custom-policy-definitions`. Repo and Learn disagree (c4bc6f10 private-DNS DINE and d45520cb Search local-auth DINE are not on Learn) → say so in notes. Keep scratch JSON in `deck/out/` (not /tmp).
Full story: `lgu-easm-rollout/deck/sections/pol.js` (3 slides, 07 pol).

## 2026-11-10 — SUCCESS PATTERN: Foundry "can we lower content filters?" has three layers — thresholds, output-off approval, enforcement

**Symptom:** Guardrails docs mix classic (Azure OpenAI) and new Foundry wording, Low/High labels read in opposite directions, and nothing states whether Azure Policy can *block* lowering.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Answer by layer. (1) Thresholds and input-side Off are self-serve; (2) Off/annotate-only for the four core harms on **outputs** and "modified abuse monitoring" need Microsoft approval (Limited Access forms; newest page says only account-team-managed/eligible customers, older content-filter page says "not possible to become a managed customer" → newest wins, flag [미검증]); (3) enforcement: guardrail authoring = Foundry Account Owner (`accounts/raiPolicies/write`; Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor also has it), and every built-in Cognitive Services guardrail Azure Policy (Preview) supports only Audit/Disabled — detect, not deny. Foundry Operate ▸ Compliance ▸ Create policy needs Owner/Resource Policy Contributor and supports exceptions. Hosted agents with no `rai_config` run with no guardrail and a bad policy name fails open. Defender side: from 2026-07-01 agent-level discovery/posture/threat protection moved to Agent 365 (`defender-xdr/security-for-ai/transition-agent-security-to-agent-365`); Defender for AI services still covers Foundry Models (text only), CSPM still discovers Foundry accounts/projects.
Full story: `lgu-easm-rollout/deck/sections/safe.js` (slides 06 safe).

## 2026-11-10 — SUCCESS PATTERN: "Foundry sandbox" is four different things — answer per layer, and take hosted-agent egress from the guardrails page, not the VNet page

**Symptom:** "How do we configure the Sandbox?" has no single switch. Searching only the network/VNet pages makes hosted-agent egress look like "BYO VNet + Firewall only", and Learn's tool list marks Browser automation "(preview)" while its own page says GA.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Split by layer: built-in Code Interpreter (Microsoft-managed ACA session, Hyper-V, no egress, 1h/idle 30min, not configurable), your own ACA session pool (`az containerapp sessionpool create --network-status EgressDisabled --cooldown-period --max-sessions`; MCP-enabled pool = Preview), hosted agent (per-session VM, `sessionConfiguration.idleTimeoutSeconds`), AKS Kata. Hosted-agent egress allow-list lives in the RAI policy (`raiPolicies@2026-05-15-preview` `egressPolicy`, Preview, hosted-only) -> `learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/agents/how-to/add-hosted-agent-guardrails`. Managed VNet is not offered in Korea Central. When a dedicated page and a nav list disagree, the dedicated page wins; note the mismatch in speaker notes.
Full story: `lgu-easm-rollout/deck/sections/sbx.js` (slides 04 sandbox / hosted vs builder).

## 2026-11-10 — SUCCESS PATTERN: read the built-in Azure Policy JSON (Azure/azure-policy) before claiming a Foundry control "works"

**Symptom:** Learn lists Foundry governance policies by display name only. Whether an allow-list can be bypassed, which parameters exist, and whether exemptions apply were not stated anywhere.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** `gh api repos/Azure/azure-policy/contents/built-in-policies/policyDefinitions/Cognitive%20Services` and read the rule. `[Preview] Microsoft Foundry agents and toolboxes should only use approved tools` (`e7352ad2-6c86-4a07-9573-47f67b557ba8`, mode `Microsoft.CognitiveServices.Data`) passes any tool whose `type` is in `approvedToolTypes`, so putting `mcp` there silently disables the `approvedMcpEndpoints` check. Also: no built-in policy requires an App Insights connection on a project; diagnostic-log categories on `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts` are not documented to carry prompt text (tracing → App Insights does); exemption docs don't list `Microsoft.CognitiveServices.Data`, so treat exemptions for that policy as "[미검증]". The `--params` JSON form of `az policy assignment create` is documented in `foundry/how-to/custom-policy-definition`.
Full story: `lgu-easm-rollout/deck/sections/gate.js` (slides 07 gate / how-to-implement).

## 2026-11-05 — SUCCESS PATTERN: verify Azure doc claims with read-only ARM/Monitor probes before trusting (or "[미검증]"-tagging) them

**Symptom:** A fine-tuning deploy guide carried "[미검증]" tags for the SKU spelling (`Developer` vs `DeveloperTier`), the management api-version (`2024-10-21` in a Learn curl example), the Azure Monitor deployment dimension name, FT quota and idle-deployment detection — all guessable only from docs that contradict each other.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Most of it is answerable read-only on any existing Azure OpenAI/Foundry account: `az cognitiveservices model list -l <region>` (per-region FT SKU names, default capacity, `deprecation` dates), `az cognitiveservices usage list -l <region>` (`…-finetune` quota buckets), `az monitor metrics list-definitions` (dimension names such as `ModelDeploymentName`), `az rest --method get` on the deployments URL with candidate api-versions (the error lists the registered ones — `2024-10-21` is data-plane only, management needs e.g. `2024-10-01`), `az bicep build` + `az deployment group validate/what-if` (non-mutating; a fake model ID is fine but proves only template/SKU shape), and the public Retail Prices API (`prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices`, supports `currencyCode=KRW`) for hosting meters. Gotchas: Azure Monitor omits deployments with zero requests instead of reporting 0 (idle = in the deployment list but absent from the metric result), and dimension values can be lower-cased (`MAI-Thinking-1` → `mai-thinking-1`) — join case-insensitively and treat a failed query as "unknown", never "idle".
Full story: `gpt54-mini-finetuning/samples/e_cleanup.sh`, `e_deploy_rest.sh`, `e_deploy.bicep`, `deck/sections/e.js` (e03/e05/e08/e12). Pause (`deploymentState=Paused`, 2026-01-15-preview) is documented to block inference with 423, but no doc says whether hosting billing stops — that stayed "[미검증]".

## 2026-11-04 — SUCCESS PATTERN: label AI-generated slide art with real PPTX text boxes driven by per-image fraction specs

**Symptom:** The 65 right-hand panel images of the Claude on Foundry deck showed components/flows with no labels; baking text into the image model output is unreliable for Korean.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Keep label specs outside the slide code (`deck/labels/*.json`, keyed by the image key, `x`/`y` as fractions of the panel; `ax`/`ay` pick edge anchors) and let `lib.js addLabels()` (called from `base()`) draw editable rounded-rect pills, so `node build.js` reproduces the labelled deck. Place each label from what is actually visible (grid-overlay contact sheet of the PNGs, then check the render), not from the prompt: AI art often drops or swaps elements and even draws wrong badges (f03 dots, f06/f14 check marks), which a pill can cover. Put pills on box edges, inside-bottom or in blank margins, never over arrow origins; give tone per element. LibreOffice adds stray spaces around `·`/`( )` and in Korean, so keep ~15% width slack. `qa_check.py` must skip `ImgLabel*` shapes in its generic overflow checks and instead flag labels <9pt, outside the panel or overlapping each other. The checked-in pptx had been re-saved by PowerPoint; rebuilding from the generator gave identical text/notes (verified with python-pptx), but check this before overwriting.
Full story: `claude-on-foundry/deck/lib.js`, `deck/labels/`, `deck/qa_check.py`.

## 2026-11-04 — SUCCESS PATTERN: patch transitive dependencies without vendoring node_modules

**Symptom:** Dependabot flagged `image-size` in `voicelive-llm-fault/deck/package-lock.json`; `pptxgenjs@4.0.1` still requests vulnerable `image-size@^1.2.1`.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Use a scoped npm override for `pptxgenjs` -> `image-size@^2.0.3`, rather than adding an unrelated direct dependency. Ignore `node_modules/` repository-wide and untrack existing copies with `git rm --cached` (preserves local files); commit the manifest and lockfile, and restore dependencies with `npm ci`. Verify with `npm ls image-size`, `npm audit`, and a full deck build to a temporary output; the patched package requires Node.js >=18.
Full story: `.gitignore`, `voicelive-llm-fault/deck/package.json`, `voicelive-llm-fault/deck/package-lock.json`.

## 2026-11-03 — SUCCESS PATTERN: generate AI panel art at the exact panel ratio and quantize it

**Symptom:** Panel images generated at 768x1344 and center-cropped to the 4.1x6.1in slide panel clipped the top/bottom icons on about a third of the slides; raw 1.1 MB PNGs also made the 65-panel deck 71 MB.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Ask the image model for the exact panel ratio (768x1143) and put "keep ~10% empty margin on all four sides" in the style prompt instead of cropping afterwards. Quantize flat-art PNGs to 256 colors (FASTOCTREE, no dither, keep alpha) for ~70 KB each (deck 6.8 MB). Keep raws in a gitignored folder and add a `--recrop` mode so re-tuning never costs API calls. The MAI image endpoint shares one 429 rate limit, so parallel processes give no speedup (about 25 s per image); run one resumable process.
Full story: `claude-on-foundry/deck/gen_images.py`.

## 2026-11-03 — SUCCESS PATTERN: let the slide author re-run the excerpts under the README's own environment

**Symptom:** Mock tests for `ex06` were green, yet a section author who exported `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE` exactly as the sample README says hit `ValueError: base_url and resource are mutually exclusive` (the sample also passed `endpoint=`), and `postgres_persistence` returned two *context managers* rather than a usable saver/store. Tests passed because the env var was never set and the Postgres path was never executed.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Have the doc author (a fresh reader) actually run each excerpt with the documented env vars, and report sample bugs instead of papering over them in the notes. Fix the sample, add a regression test (`monkeypatch.setenv` both env paths; assert the helper is a `_GeneratorContextManager`), then update the slide excerpt, its notes and every test-count mention. Library env-var fallbacks (`ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE`) silently conflict with explicit constructor args, so pass the endpoint explicitly only when the env var is absent.
Full story: `claude-on-foundry/samples/ex06_langgraph_agent.py`, `tests/test_langgraph.py`, e02/e05 slides.

## 2026-11-03 — FAILURE ROUTE: one Python environment for Claude on Foundry with both MAF and LangChain

**Symptom:** `pip install agent-framework-anthropic langchain-azure-ai` cannot resolve: `agent-framework-anthropic 1.0.0b261030` needs `anthropic>=1.11,<2`, `langchain-azure-ai 1.2.12` needs `anthropic<1.0`. Anthropic SDK 1.x also moved its HTTP layer to `httpx2`, so passing an `httpx.Client` as `http_client=` raises `TypeError`, and SDK 0.125 has no typed `compaction=` argument on `beta.messages.create` (1.17 has it).
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Keep two virtualenvs/containers (`requirements-maf.txt`, `requirements-langchain.txt`), inject `httpx2.Client`/`MockTransport` on 1.x, use `extra_body` for new beta fields on 0.x. `AsyncAnthropicFoundry` needs an *async* token provider (`azure.identity.aio`); `psycopg` without libpq fails with "no pq wrapper available" -> `psycopg[binary,pool]`.
Full story: `claude-on-foundry/samples/README.md`, troubleshooting slide of `Claude_on_Foundry_Agents_Handbook_KO.pptx`.

## 2026-11-03 — SUCCESS PATTERN: test Foundry-hosted Claude agents with no Azure credentials

**Symptom:** No Foundry subscription or key was available, yet the deck needed code-level samples that were actually executed.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Build the real SDK client (`AnthropicFoundry`, MAF `AnthropicFoundryClient`, `AzureAIAnthropicChatModel`) with a `base_url` pointing at the production URL shape and a scripted `MockTransport` handler. Assert the *request* (path `/anthropic/v1/messages`, `x-api-key`/`api-key` headers, `thinking: {type: adaptive}` + `output_config.effort`, no `budget_tokens`) and play back tool_use/tool_result turns. For LangGraph use a tiny fake `BaseChatModel` with `bind_tools`. Label every snippet in the deck as Mock-tested / signature-only / illustrative; never imply live Foundry calls.
Full story: `claude-on-foundry/samples/tests/`.

## 2026-11-03 — SUCCESS PATTERN: give a stateless model memory without a native memory service

**Symptom:** Claude on Foundry is a Marketplace partner model; Agent Service prompt agents and Foundry managed Memory (Azure OpenAI chat + embedding deployments required) are not documented for it.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Layer it: Anthropic client-side `memory` tool backed by Blob/Cosmos (`BetaAbstractMemoryTool`, tenant-scoped keys, strict `/memories` path validation), prompt caching + context editing + on-demand compaction for the working window, LangGraph checkpointer + Store, a MAF `ContextProvider`, Foundry Memory used as an external service with GPT as the extractor. The user/tenant id always comes from the authenticated principal, never from model output; stored facts are injected as data, not instructions.
Full story: `claude-on-foundry/samples/` (ex02-ex07) and the memory section of the deck.

## 2026-11-03 — SUCCESS PATTERN: compare models by cost per task, not price per token

**Symptom:** Sonnet 5.5 ($2/$10 per 1M) looked cheaper than Opus 5.5 ($4/$20) but Artificial Analysis measured $7.60 vs $5.98 per task at max effort because it emitted ~193K vs ~119K output tokens; vendor Terminal-Bench 4.0 (66.4%) differed from the independent harness (59.6%).
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Always show vendor-reported vs independent numbers separately with harness/effort/date, plot cost per task, and tag secondary aggregators as lower confidence. Benchmarks that render client-side may need the raw HTML parsed instead of a markdown conversion. Check commercial blockers before architecture: Claude on Foundry is Marketplace-billed (MACC-eligible, no Microsoft/STU discount) and Enterprise accounts in South Korea are listed as unsupported.
Full story: benchmark and commercial sections of `Claude_on_Foundry_Agents_Handbook_KO.pptx`.

## 2026-10-23 — SUCCESS PATTERN: pin the model guide, not the "latest" landing page

**Symptom:** OpenAI's unqualified `guides/latest-model` returned GPT-6 guidance while preparing a GPT-5.4-mini document; an older cookbook link also redirected.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Read the exact model page first and use `guides/latest-model?model=gpt-5.4` for generation-specific guidance. Never carry the latest model's defaults, context limits or supported settings into an older variant.
Full story: `GPT_5_4_Mini_Tuning_Guide_KO.pptx`, model-contract and source-register slides.

## 2026-10-23 — SUCCESS PATTERN: type-check Responses history round trips

**Symptom:** With the installed TypeScript SDK, spreading `response.output` directly into `ResponseInput` failed type-checking because the output and input unions differ.
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** Use the SDK's `toResponseInputItems` helper from `openai/lib/responses/ResponseInputItems`, then preserve the complete converted output before appending `function_call_output` items. Do not hide the mismatch with `any` or discard reasoning/history items.
Full story: `GPT_5_4_Mini_Tuning_Guide_KO.pptx`, TypeScript tool-results slide and its complete speaker-note example.

## Success pattern: rebuilding a Korean PPTX with generated images (2026-10)
- Generate images portrait (768x1344, MAI-Image-2.6-Flash), then center-crop with PIL to the exact panel ratio before inserting; pptxgenjs `cover` sizing is unreliable.
- Image calls take ~15s each and hit 429; run the skill's client sequentially in the background and skip existing files so it is resumable.
- pptxgenjs table/card fonts look much smaller than intended at 8-10pt on a 13.33in slide; render via soffice -> pdftoppm and scale fonts up until tables fill ~70% of the height without touching the footer.
- `validate.py` reports a `notesMasterIdLst` ordering error for pptxgenjs output; it is a known generator quirk, not a content bug.
- A native 2D bar chart can also contain an undeclared third series `axId` (the generator emits the 3D reference unconditionally). Compare references with declared `catAx`/`valAx`/`serAx`, remove only the orphan from the 2D chart, and revalidate both XML and cached chart values. Do not remove a valid 3D axis.

## Investigation pattern: how a Foundry agent really uses knowledge (2026-10)
- List agents with `GET {project}/agents?api-version=v1&limit=100` (bearer scope `https://ai.azure.com`); read `versions.latest.definition.tools` for `mcp` server_url / `file_search`. A KB MCP URL is `{search}/knowledgebases/{kb}/mcp`.
- Verify each link: `GET {search}/knowledgebases` (bearer scope `https://search.azure.com`), `/knowledgesources`, `/indexes/{i}/stats`, `/indexers/{n}/status`, and ARM `projects/{p}/connections`. Agents can reference a deleted KB or a Search host that no longer resolves, and an indexer can report success with 0 items.
- The service masks connection strings and keys in knowledge source/data source GETs, so the storage account behind a blob source cannot be read back directly.

## Investigation pattern: reading a Voice Live browser event log (2026-10)
- The `/mai-live` raw-event panel logs browser-receive times (`new Date()`), only server→browser events, and truncates `audio.delta` to 119 chars, so delta size/duration is not in the log. Reproduce live with the same voice (`pre_generated_assistant_message`, no LLM) to measure it: chunks are 9,600 → 14,400 → 24,000 B (200/300/500 ms), the first ~14 burst in ~160 ms, then one 500 ms chunk per ~167 ms (3x real time).
- Audio length ≈ `usage.output_token_details.audio_tokens` × 50 ms (within 0.4–1.3%); use it to cross-check the chunk model against the log.
- `response.done` / `audio.done` mean generated/sent, not heard. `browser-audio-player.ts` schedules sequentially (`startAt = max(nextStartTime, currentTime)`), so the audible tail = audio length − delivery time (+38.2 s here), and `auto_truncate` assumes real-time playback. Map audio-clock to wall-clock with `audio_start_ms + prefix_padding` (judgment time) using several events; check the spread.
- A TTS-only repro plus an STT round trip showed the TTS reads URLs and markdown aloud — compare screen text length with audio length before trusting the transcript.
- Dead ends: STT word offsets from faster-than-realtime audio injection were unreliable, and `output_audio_timestamp_types: ["word"]` returned no `audio_timestamp` events.

## Success pattern: Korean forensic timeline deck from a log (2026-10)
- Draw timelines as native pptxgenjs shapes driven by a parsed `analysis.json` (exact positions, every event); keep the generated infographic on the right panel. Tables: `margin` is in inches; rising `line` shapes need `flipV`.
- Generated infographic text is unreliable (typos like "Serve stream", unreadable small labels): prompt with a few huge exact labels, then verify every label visually.
- Reviewers/renders use fallback fonts (LibreOffice has no Malgun Gothic), so stray spaces around Latin/Hangul are render artifacts; judge overlaps, clipped labels and dashed lines through text instead.
- Fix the `notesMasterIdLst` quirk by moving it right after `sldMasterIdLst` in `ppt/presentation.xml`; `validate.py` then passes.

## Success pattern: comparing voice STT APIs without crossing contracts (2026-10)
- Bind every capability, retirement, processing scope and price to host + route + model + region + date. File-result SSE is not microphone streaming, and a native-audio model's optional transcript is not necessarily its reasoning input.
- Azure Retail Prices can return no rows under an obsolete service name and mark valid standard meters non-primary. Cross-check the official regional price table and exact model; a primary promotional meter is not the generic service rate.
- Keep direct OpenAI model retirements separate from Azure-hosted availability. See `VoiceLive_STT_Engineering_Report.pptx` for the source-qualified comparison and explicit benchmark/access gaps.

## Failure route: trusting WorkIQ's shell exit status (2026-10)
- WorkIQ can exit zero while returning JSON `isError: true`. Inspect the response before counting retrieved intranet sources.
- An unsupported OAuth redirect is an authentication gap, not evidence that no relevant documents exist. Record zero successful sources; do not relabel prior repository documents as live SharePoint/Teams research.

## Success pattern: Microsoft-Decision-1 (systemone) usage package (2026-10)
- Contract (verified live): `POST {endpoint}/providers/microsoft/v1/systemone`; request `model` is the **deployment name** (wrong name → 404 `DeploymentNotFound`, docs say 422); the response nests results under **`answers`** (`{model, answers:{name:{…}}, usage}`), so parse `payload["answers"][name]`. A choice needs 2–255 options; empty `questions` and unknown types return 400. Output tokens are free but non-zero. `confidence` can differ from the top probability.
- It is not a chat model: in Foundry Agents use it as a client-side **function tool** or as a **gate/router** in front of the agent. In tool mode a prompt only *asks* the model to call the tool, so make the **code** decide: no valid triage result or `action != "proceed"` → discard the LLM text and hand off. Azure's own prompt-shield filter may reject classic injections with HTTP 400 `content_filter` before the agent runs; catch it and treat it as a block.
- Question wording moved one gate from 90% to 100% ("promise a refund?" read as future-only). Tuned and scored on the same 20 items, so label it in-sample. Never write "statistically indistinguishable" from n=40 without paired predictions and a test.
- Security-review found that `urllib.request.urlopen` follows redirects and re-sends `Authorization`/`api-key`, bypassing a host allow-list. Use an opener whose `redirect_request` returns `None`; test it with two real local servers and confirm the test fails without the fix.
- Wrap response parsing so every malformed shape raises the documented exception, not `AttributeError`/`ValueError`.
- Image generation (MAI-Image-2.6-Flash): about 12 s between calls, run sequentially. Bar charts get false proportions, so use tiles or label "not to scale". 8% top/bottom margins plus "no title text" stop cropping and invented titles. Wait on a PID with `kill -0`; `pgrep -f` matches its own shell.
- pptxgenjs emits one `<a:pPr>` per text run (schema-invalid after the first run), and `validate.py` does not flag it; strip extras with JSZip, and put paragraph options on the first run only. Also move `notesMasterIdLst` right after `sldMasterIdLst`, after which `validate.py` passes.
- LibreOffice grows table rows past `rowH`: budget `head + n×rowH` plus slack before the next shape. That arithmetic caused overlaps on two slides.
- Evidence: `mai-decision-1/` (skill, `test-results/`, `deck/build_deck.js`). The numbers are a 40-ticket synthetic sample, not a benchmark.

## Success pattern: Voice Live PTU 500 diagnosis deck, built with parallel authors (2026-11)
- Premise check first: the customer believed "500 is never spilled over". The Learn spillover page (2026-06-18) says spillover triggers on 429, long-context 400 and 500/503 **when configured** (`spilloverDeploymentName` or `x-ms-spillover-deployment`, same resource/model/version). Correct the premise in the deck and list why 500s may still surface (not configured, no standard quota, mid-stream failure, stall, failure outside the PTU, BYOM RBAC). Whether spillover is honoured through Voice Live BYOM is undocumented: label it unverified, never imply it works.
- Voice Live has no `response.failed` event (failure = `response.done` with `status:"failed"`), `session.update` cannot change the model (failover = close WS and reconnect with new `model=`), and no documented request-id link from a Voice Live session to the downstream PTU request. `metadata` is the best correlation key. Verify event questions against the reference HTML (`curl` + strip tags) when research reports disagree (`rate_limits.updated` is in the reference).
- Research subagents may be unable to write files: have them return the report text and save it yourself. Tag every claim [문서]/[추정]/[미검증] in the deck.
- Fleet pattern that worked: write `lib.js` + a SPEC.md (rules, facts, module contract), generate placeholder panels (`images_ph/`, real images win), then run 5 section authors in parallel (each `sections/<id>.js` + `prompts/<id>.json`, `node build.js --only <id>`), generate all panels sequentially in the background (~25 s each with 429 waits), then 3 fresh-eyes QA agents over slide ranges.
- Panel regeneration fixes: ask for "light paper-colored boxes with dark ink text" (dark boxes gave 1.2:1 contrast), spell tricky labels letter by letter ("recv" came out "recev"), forbid empty boxes, and say "ALL checkboxes ticked" when the slide says done.
- Slogans must not contradict the content (an ending line promised "automatic failover" while the deck says none exists).
- pptxgenjs native charts write `<c:v></c:v>` for `null` values (gaps), which risks invalid XML in PowerPoint: for series with missing levels use separate single-series charts instead. It also mutates the option objects you pass, so build fresh options per `addChart` call. Per-bar colors need a single series with several `chartColors`. Run `soffice` with `-env:UserInstallation=` pointing inside the project when `/tmp` is off-limits, and delete that profile dir afterwards.

## Success pattern: researching a learning/certification path with unfetchable sites (2026-11)
- Enumerate Learn content with the catalog API (`learn.microsoft.com/api/catalog/?type=learningPaths&product=<product>`): it gives exact slugs, module counts and minutes. Guessed path slugs often 404, so take them from that JSON. Cert pages and study guides give exam length, renewal and Korean availability.
- `community.fabric.microsoft.com`, `blog.fabric.microsoft.com` and `learn.palantir.com` return 403 to fetchers and `roadmap.fabric.microsoft.com` is JS-rendered. Use search snippets only as a second source and tag the item [미검증] in the slide and in refs.
- `gh api repos/<o>/<r>` gives stars and push date; many plausible repo names (fabric-ontology, fabric-dojo, fabric-mcp) are 404, so verify each before bookmarking.
- `qa_check.py` treats text at y ≤ 6.7in as body, but `lib.base()` draws the 10pt source caption at y=6.6 (2 lines). Wrap `L.base` so the caption is added at y=6.71, h=0.31 (as sections a/b/h do), otherwise every slide gets a "10pt text" error.
- Table cells in `L.table` have ~0.1in margins: a 0.4–0.45in column wraps two-digit numbers and the header "순서", and the grown rows push a 15-row table over the footer. Use ≥0.55–0.6in.

## Success pattern: Fabric IQ / ontology / agents / lineage research from Learn only (2026-11)
- Learn pages fetched in bulk with a small requests+BeautifulSoup script (text to a gitignored `out/` folder, log `url, status, ms.date, updated_at`) are much cheaper than `web_fetch`, which prepends long frontmatter. Guessed slugs 404 often (`data-agent-mcp`, `graph/glossary`, `purview/data-map-lineage`); take real ones from each page's TOC and list only HTTP 200 URLs in `refs/`.
- Status is per feature and mixed: ontology and Graph are preview, Data agent is GA but its ontology/Graph sources are preview, Operations agent has no preview label on its main page but the region table mixes "(preview)". State each separately; Maps and per-feature Korea Central availability of ontology are undocumented → [미검증].
- Korea capacities use cross-geo Azure OpenAI processing (US/EU Data Boundary hosting), so Copilot and data agents need the cross-geo tenant settings. Legacy Foundry data-agent integration ends 2026-11-06 (use the Fabric IQ / OneLake catalog tool). The old ontology experience ends 2027-01-31.
- Purview Fabric-lineage docs are old (ms.date 2025): lakehouse sub-item lineage is unsupported, there is no cross-workspace lineage, and column-level lineage exists only for Power BI ↔ Azure SQL/Blob/ADLS. Fabric's own lineage view has no per-item-type table and no column-level lineage, so say so instead of guessing.
- `L.callout` only knows tones clay|azure|moss|amber; any other (e.g. `fab`) yields `"" is not a valid scheme color` and a black box with unreadable text. A `build.js` warning like that is a render bug, not noise.

## Success pattern: Fabric security/network research (PL, OAP, MPE, TWA, CMK) from Learn only (2026-11)
- Preview/GA is per page, not per feature family: workspace IP firewall (title says preview), OAP for .pbix reports, Real-Time Events OAP, Eventstream MPE, SQL database under workspace PL, OneLake security third-party engines and CMK for Eventhouse/BYOK models carry preview markers; tenant/workspace PL, OAP for DE/DF/DW/OneLake/semantic models and OneLake security carry none (write "프리뷰 표기 없음", GA is [미검증]); Trusted workspace access and workspace identity are explicitly GA.
- Constraints worth leading with: workspace PL and OAP are F SKU only (no Trial), workspace PL cannot cover workspaces with semantic models, on-prem data gateway cannot register under tenant PL (use VNet data gateway), OAP does not stop exfiltration through inbound requests, and ADLS/Blob shortcuts via MPE are unsupported under OAP. IP firewall excludes OneLake security, Power BI and Copilot.
- Compliance: the Learn offering pages give K-ISMS (Azure Korea infrastructure, 80 controls), CSAP (Azure IaaS low tier, 2024-11-20) and a FedRAMP scope table that lists Microsoft Fabric; Fabric-specific K-ISMS/CSAP/ISO/SOC coverage is not stated, so mark it [미검증] rather than inferring from the Azure-level certificate.
- Competitive/benchmark research (section e): G2, Gartner (documents/*, Peer Insights) and TrustRadius return 403 to fetchers, and Gartner/Forrester Leader lists are paywalled, so take placements only from vendor blogs/web_search snippets and tag them [벤더]; never state a vendor's quadrant position you did not see. Databricks has no object/link/action ontology (Genie Ontology = UC metric views + inferred snippets, Public Preview); Fabric IQ Ontology has no documented Palantir-style action model (write-back is translytical task flows), so tag the Ontology→action link [미검증]. Compare only like-for-like benchmarks: the audited Databricks TPC-DS 100TB record (2021), Fabric's native-engine claim (vs OSS Spark, not Photon) and the personal GitHub 3TB POC are not comparable.
- Mechanics: keep scratch research text under `deck/out/research_c/` (not /tmp) and delete it at the end; `pdftoppm` file names are zero-padded when a deck has ≥10 slides (`c-01.png`); superscript footnote marks (¹²³) render as stray apostrophes in LibreOffice, so use plain digits in matrix cells.

## Success pattern: 9-author fleet for a 180-slide Korean handbook deck (2026-11)
- Order that worked: shared `lib.js` + `SPEC.md` (tags, section map, module contract) → 9 parallel authors each owning only `sections/<id>.js`, `prompts/<id>.json`, `refs/<id>.json` → sequential MAI image generation in ONE background process (resumable, ~15–20 s/image, 135 prompts ≈ 50 min; placeholders in `images_ph/` keep builds working) → 4 parallel fresh-eyes QA fixers (render → view → fix → `build.js --only`) → full rebuild + `qa_check.py`.
- Shared-lib drift is the main cross-author friction: `qa_check.py` footer threshold (6.55) vs `lib.base()` source caption (y=6.6), and `callout/steps/head` rejecting new tone names. Fix once in lib/QA, not per section. QA fixers repeatedly found the same classes: Latin words breaking mid-word in table cells (add spaces around slashes/arrows), orphaned ▲/✅ glyphs, wrong tone colours (clay=Databricks, amber=unverified/negative, azure=neutral), tables ending past y≈6.5.
- Appendix generated from `refs/*.json` must show the FULL URL (two-line rows, strip scheme and `en-us/`, ~10 rows/page, dedupe by URL); a 46-char truncated URL column was useless (45 pages for 424 refs is fine).
- WorkIQ failure route: on a headless server `workiq ask`/`auth login` fails with MSAL "Only loopback redirect uri is supported" and there is no cached credential. Do not retry variants (`--account`, `-t`, older versions, fake browser). Bridge: commit `workiq/run_workiq.sh` that writes `results.md`, have the user run it on their Mac (older workiq lacks `--no-streaming`), `git pull`, merge as [WorkIQ]. Until then count zero WorkIQ sources and say so in the appendix.

## Success pattern: labelling AI images in an existing pptx that has no generator (2026-11)
- `GPT_5_4_Mini_Tuning_Guide_KO.pptx` has no source folder: edit it with python-pptx. Keep a spec of `(text, x%, y%)` per slide relative to the picture box, name shapes `ImgLabel_N`, delete `ImgLabel_*` first so a re-run is idempotent, and render all slides with `soffice` + `pdftoppm` to check them.
- Read positions by viewing grid contact sheets of the extracted media (percent ticks), not from alt text; use alt text, slide text and title only for what each element means. Mark unclear icons as unlabelled instead of guessing.
- Size pills from a char-width estimate (Hangul and circled digits ①–⑤ = 1.0 em, Latin ≈ 0.6) plus ~18% slack: LibreOffice swaps in another font and inserts stray spaces in Korean. A 3.5in-wide picture holds ~3 pills per row, so stagger y.
- python-pptx `save()` rewrote this deck's non-standard `Default jpg = image/jpg` into 62 per-part Overrides and `validate.py` then FAILED on content types. Collapse them back to one `Default jpg = image/jpeg` after saving (done in the script).
- Don't name a helper `inspect.py` (shadows the stdlib); with `/tmp` off-limits keep renders and the LibreOffice profile in a scratch dir inside the repo and delete it afterwards.
- Visual-QA fixes go into the script, not the pptx: `ADJUST` (slide → label n → x/y/w in inches) applies QA nudges on top of the % SPEC, and re-running on the current pptx is idempotent. Shrinking a pill to clear an icon can make LibreOffice (wider Latin fallback) wrap it ("mediu/m", "추론·프롬프트"): set `wrap: False` or keep ≥ the rendered text width. Re-render after every width change. Pills that carry "①–⑥" must not reuse the digits of the body-text list (slide 61 conflict): drop the digits instead.

## Success pattern: fine-tuning data section with runnable scripts (gpt54-mini-finetuning section b, 2026-11)
- Ship a synthetic generator first (`b_make_synthetic_tickets.py`, seed 42) plus a dirty copy with N injected defects; then the validator's "caught N/N" output is a real [실측] slide and every other script can run without customer data.
- Hangul in NFD (jamo split) is ~10× the tokens of NFC (43 vs 4 for "환불해 주세요"): normalise to NFC before counting or uploading. Count tokens with tiktoken `o200k_base` if importable, else a heuristic (+4% off here); tiktoken needs a writable `TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR` inside the repo (no /tmp).
- Split AFTER dedup and mask digits when checking near-duplicates: ticket templates that differ only in order numbers leak across splits (63 near-dups); masking them in the group key fixes leakage but skews category ratios, so report both.
- Reasoning-model chat calls use the `developer` role and `max_completion_tokens` (no temperature/top_p); the docs recommend the v1 `OpenAI(base_url=.../openai/v1/)` client over `AzureOpenAI` + api-version.
- Rendering: `∩` is missing in LibreOffice's Consolas fallback and shows as a stray `n`; use `&` or words in code blocks.

## Success pattern: 4-deck visual-QA fleet + label-before-image mismatch (2026-11)
- Labels written in panel fractions BEFORE the MAI image exists never line up: the generator draws boxes lower/wider than the prompt's percentages. Fix = per-section QA agents that MEASURE the real box rectangles from the PNG and re-place each label (v2 a–h, Fabric a–j,z), not tweak by eye. Better: generate images first, then author labels.
- Fan-out shape that worked on a 2-core box: one agent per section (own file only, `node build.js --only <id>` writes out/<id>.pptx so no output races); decks with a single editable pptx (no generator) get REPORT-ONLY inspectors plus ONE fixer to avoid concurrent saves.
- Panels with 8–12 pastel-tone labels failed contrast (2.3–3.4:1): use navy/white pills on busy panels.
- pptxgenjs BAR charts fail `validate.py` (dPt written after dLbls in `<c:ser>`; 2D `<c:barChart>` has a 3rd `<c:axId>` pointing at an undeclared serAx). FIXED in both decks' `build.js` by `pptx-tools/chart_schema_order.js` (lossless reorder + drop the dangling axId); `validate.py` is now a clean PASS, so treat any chart error as real. Line/area/radar/scatter/bubble have non-ordering pptxgenjs defects the helper does not cover.
- Never `git stash` while background agents edit the tree.

## Success pattern: clearing [미검증] eval-SDK items by introspection (gpt54-mini-finetuning section f, 2026-11)
- Verify SDK names by installing the real package in a venv inside the repo and introspecting (`inspect.signature`, enum members, model fields), not by reading docs alone. Findings: evaluator/grader deployment key is `initialization_parameters["model"]` (`deployment_name` only in custom prompt-evaluator schemas); `azure-ai-evaluation` safety evaluators take `threshold=` (default 3) locally; `AttackStrategy` members are in `azure.ai.evaluation.red_team`, and `[redteam]` needs `pyrit==0.11.0` (pyrit 1.x breaks the import).
- A bare `%` in an argparse `help=` string crashes `--help` (`ValueError: unsupported format character`): write `%%`. Run `--help` on every script after editing, not only the main path.
- "No retirement notice in the docs" cannot prove "not retiring": keep [미검증] with the attempts listed. Price assumptions in a deck are checkable read-only via `prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices` (`serviceName eq 'Foundry Models'`); gpt-4.1-mini FT hosting was $1.70/h, so an H=$1 break-even was off by 70%.
- Entra token auth was enough for a ≤5-request live smoke (judge + runner) and read-only `evals.list`; state-changing `evals.create` stays unrun when no fine-tuned deployment exists.

## Success pattern: clearing [미검증] Foundry items with read-only az/REST (gpt54-mini-finetuning section c, 2026-11)
- Resolve doc-vs-doc disagreements on roles with `az role definition list --name <GUID>` (dataActions vs actions/notDataActions): Foundry Project Manager has data `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/*` but no `accounts/deployments/write`, so the RBAC table (can run FT, cannot deploy) is right and the authn page is loose. Account Owner has empty dataActions.
- `GET /openai/v1/models` on Azure = the region's BASE-MODEL catalog (539 entries, each with `capabilities{fine_tune, global_fine_tune, devtier_fine_tune}` + `lifecycle_status`), not the account's deployments. Read the extras via `m.model_dump()`.
- Standard-training regions are not documented; infer them read-only from `.../modelCapacities?modelName=..&modelVersion=..` → `availableFinetuneCapacity` per SKU (Korea Central had only GlobalStandard/Developer for gpt-4.1-mini). Tier from `.../quotaTiers?api-version=2025-10-01-preview`; FT counters `OpenAI.<SKU>.<model>-finetune` appear in `az cognitiveservices usage list`.
- Dead ends: `az cognitiveservices account update --help` (2.91.0) has no disable-local-auth / public-network-access flag (use ARM/Bicep/PowerShell); `account list-usage` returned 0 items on an AIServices account. An account with `disableLocalAuth=true` gives HTTP 401 for any API key, so run the preflight with `--auth entra`.

## Success pattern: clearing [미검증] Fabric handbook items (sections a–e, 2026-11-05)
- Fastest evidence = raw markdown from the docs repo: `gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" repos/MicrosoftDocs/fabric-docs/contents/docs/<path>.md` (check `ms.date`), grep it locally; far quicker than rendering learn.microsoft.com. `admin/region-availability.md` has a per-region "Not available" column (Korea Central empty; Korea South = Power BI only).
- Retail Prices API has NO per-SKU Fabric meter: PAYG is per workload "<x> Capacity Usage CU" (KC 280.9 KRW/CU·h = 0.21 USD vs East US 0.18), reservations are per CU per term (1y 1,463,389 / 3y 4,390,167 KRW, ≈40.5% off), "OD On-Demand"/overage meters (from 2026-10-01) are 3× PAYG. F64 = 64 × CU price. `az rest GET /subscriptions/<sub>/providers/Microsoft.Fabric/skus?api-version=2023-11-01` lists F2…F8192 for a region, but SKU listing ≠ workload availability.
- Fabric docs contradict each other on status: IP firewall (admin-portal doc says preview, overview doesn't), Native Execution Engine (overview "preview" vs Runtime 1.3/2.0 built-in), OAP/CMK GA. Cite both, keep [미검증] and record "확인 시도/결과" instead of picking one.
- Learn compliance offering pages (K-ISMS, CSAP, SOC 2) don't list per-service scope; Fabric scope lives only in STP certificates → keep [미검증]. Home-region change is not self-service (Support tenant remap deletes data); the alternative is Multi-Geo.
- Dead ends: Gartner/Forrester/G2 pages are paywalled/403; "no doc mentions X" (ontology action types, column-level lineage) is absence of evidence, not proof — leave [미검증] with the search recorded.
- Never run a global `sed -i` for a "one-line" tag change: the same suffix existed on another slide's source line (d.js lineage slide) and was flipped too; use `edit` with a unique anchor.

## Success pattern: regenerate-then-measure panel images + rubber-duck QA (all four decks, 2026-11-05)
- A panel image that disagrees with its slide (6 boxes vs 7 steps, 8-column grid vs 7×12 table, 6 Q/A rows vs 7 FAQ items, 3 diamonds vs 4 decision steps) cannot be fixed by labels: rewrite the prompt with exact counts and normalised box rectangles ("exactly seven boxes, no more, no fewer"), delete `images/<n>.png` + `images/raw/<n>.png`, rerun `gen_images.py` (one generator process at a time), VIEW the result, only then place labels from PIL-measured rectangles. All four came out right on the first attempt with explicit counts.
- The 14-agent fleet finished in ~55 min on 2 cores with one image generator; keep verifiers off the shared image endpoint and tell every agent "touch only your slide block" to avoid edit races in shared section files.
- rubber-duck caught real problems the authors missed: an internal-only WorkIQ conclusion (J8) quoted on a customer-facing FAQ slide, contradictory test counts (28 vs 29) between a source line and its notes, and a [실측] tag on a value that was only multiplied (price × 64) — tag derived numbers as 계산. A "bug" report quoting `Authorization: ******` was display masking of `Bearer ${TOKEN}`: grep the raw bytes (`od -c`) before "fixing" a redacted-looking line.
- New decks' `deck/out/` and `deck/images/raw/` are build scratch: gitignored via `/*/deck/out/` and `/*/deck/images/raw/` (already-tracked voicelive files stay tracked).

## Failure route: data-bearing glyphs in panel images (Fabric c10/e10/f06, 2026-11-05)
- Never let the image prompt draw check/cross/hourglass cells, star rows, traffic-light dots or bars of unequal size: the model invents values that contradict the slide table (✔ grid vs table, 5★/3.5★/1★ vs 4.6/4.6/4.2, 3 green dots on "낮음"). Prompt for EMPTY cells / identical neutral cards and put every value in real text (table or label).
- The model miscounts grids: with a header-icon list it put the plug icon in the empty corner (7 columns, not 8) or added a 13th data row. Spell out "exactly 13 rows (never 14), corner cell empty, icons in columns 2-8", list row icons in table order (they stay visible beside labels, so icon↔row meaning must match), and just re-roll 2-3 candidates (~12 s each) into the session `files/` dir and pick the correct one by counting PIL-measured grid lines.
- pptxgenjs `margin` on label text boxes is in POINTS (≈0), so a label box width is the usable text width; qa_check's "may overflow" warnings for 3-letter pills are conservative — trust the LibreOffice render.

## Success pattern: FHIR/DICOM section b (FHIR 상세) build + render loop (2026-11-05)
- `qa_check.py` does NOT detect a table growing over the code block below it or into the footer (LibreOffice grows wrapped rows). Render and view every table+code slide; fixes that worked: drop repeated prefixes like `[base]` from mono cells, widen the mono column to ≥ 0.105 in × chars + 0.2, put prose (not mono) in cells that must wrap, and shrink `rowH`/code `y` together. Rendered page number = PNG index + 1.
- FHIR facts that bite: `Extension.url` SHALL be a URL (a `urn:` value is invalid); `fhirpathpy` returns `[]` for `ofType()` unless a model is passed; `fhir.resources` accepts `gender='f'` because bindings are not enforced (parsing ≠ validity); KR Core CodeSystems (kostat-kcd-8, hira-edi-*, kpis-kdcode) are `content=not-present`. IG root pages are language-redirect stubs: fetch `/en/<page>.html`. HAPI docs render nav-only: read the markdown via `gh api`.
- Dead end: Google Cloud SMART on FHIR support and Azure Korea Central / AWS Seoul availability were not confirmable from vendor docs; keep [미검증] instead of inferring.

## Success pattern: runnable FHIR Python samples against a stdlib mock server (healthcare-fhir-dicom section d, 2026-11)
- `http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler` writes headers and body separately; on keep-alive connections Nagle + delayed ACK stalls each request ~40 ms (48 ms/req -> 1.6 ms). Set `disable_nagle_algorithm = True` on the handler class before measuring any latency/async speed-up.
- `fhirpathpy.evaluate(res, "value")` WITHOUT the model argument silently returns `[]` for `value[x]` choice types (no error); always pass `models["r4"]`. `fhir.resources` validates structure only: `gender='fem'` passes (required code bindings are not enforced), and `model_dump()` returns `datetime.date`, so use `model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)`.
- pytest `tmp_path` lives in /tmp: use a repo-local work dir fixture plus `-p no:cacheprovider` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` where /tmp is forbidden. Quote timings as best-of-3 ranges on a shared 2-core host (same FHIRPath benchmark gave 31x, 56x and 105x); slide numbers that contradict the latest run are the usual QA finding.
- Verify slide code is a real excerpt: load `sections/<id>.js` in node with a Proxy around `../lib` capturing `L.code` lines and check every trimmed line exists in `samples/<id>_*.py` (only dedent allowed); this also catches stale edits after a sample is changed.

## Success pattern: Korean regulation facts from law.go.kr (healthcare-fhir-dicom section h, 2026-11)
- Fastest evidence = POST the statute body from `https://www.law.go.kr/법령/<이름>` (lsiSeq/efYd in the page) and strip HTML; 고시 via `/행정규칙/<이름>`; 별표 PDFs are linked as `id="pdfNNN"` and `pdftotext -layout` them. Always read the header line `[시행 … ] [법률 제…호]` and check for a 공포 후 시행 전 amendment (의료법 제23조제4항 열람기록 = 법률 제21776호, 시행 2026-12-10, still "시행 예정" while the current text says 추가기재·수정).
- Count annex rows yourself: ISMS-P 별표 7 = 80 + 21 = 101 controls, while the Azure Learn K-ISMS page implies 102 (80 + 22). State the source of each number. A CSAP Learn page "하(Low)" tier covers systems without personal data, so do not claim it covers medical workloads.
- CORRECTED dead end: 의료법 제23조제4항 접속기록 보관 위반 DOES have a penalty — 제90조 lists 제23조제4항 (500만원 이하 벌금); 제87조의2 names only 제23조제3항. Always grep the whole 벌칙 chapter (제87~제91조) before writing "벌칙 확인 못 함". 계도기간 = 과기정통부 행정 방침 (korea.kr), not a statutory grace period.
- Read 부칙 delayed-effect lists literally before dating a clause: 안전성 확보조치 기준 제6조의2 (고시 제2025-9호) is effective 2025-10-31 (발령일); only 제4조①12·13, 제5조①·⑥, 제6조②, 제8조①·② slip to 2026-10-31 (PIPC 보도자료 agrees). 정보통신망법 §48-3①·④ 후단 deems a prior report/notice under another law as done; 개인정보법 §34 and 의료법 §23-3 have no such clause → "병행 적용" is only true for those two. 개인정보법 §64-2①9호 단서 (안전조치 이행 시 제외) is the exemption, ⑨ is 가산금. History list: GET `LSW/lsHstListR.do?lsId=<id>&chrClsCd=010202` with Referer; bill status needs the 의안 progress page (search snippets = [미검증]).
- Dead ends: koshin.or.kr does not answer (EMR 인증 portal is emrcert.mohw.go.kr / khis.or.kr); mono-font law codes (A26430.01) need ≥1.3 in table column or they wrap; a 0.5 in "등급" column wraps the header and pushes the table into the callout below.

## Success pattern: measuring box rectangles for panel labels without scipy/cv2 (healthcare-fhir-dicom section g, 2026-11)
- Author-guessed GEO fractions (x .12-.88) were wrong for every image (real boxes e.g. x .171-.83): always measure. With only numpy+PIL: mask `lum>195 & sat<70` as background, label connected components with a pure-python BFS, treat the largest as outside and the rest as enclosed, then `MinFilter(15)`+`MaxFilter(15)` (opening) to drop arrows/ornaments, and read box rects from row/column runs. PIL `ImageDraw.floodfill` silently did nothing here.
- Generated panels are 764x1136, not 768x1143; use fractions. Pictograms sit bottom-right of each box, so thin boxes get a label whose right edge is the icon's left edge, tall boxes (>=1.2 in) get a top-anchored full-width label; a white pill + navy text is legible on saturated and cream boxes alike.
- Line 2 of a 2-line label must stay under ~box_width_in*72/fs Hangul chars with 15% slack; 6 of 19 labels tripped qa_check's conservative warning and shortening them (dropping qualifiers already on the slide) cleared it.

## Success pattern: section h panel labels (healthcare-fhir-dicom, 2026-11)
- Pale panels (h02) were classified as background by `lum`/`sat` alone: use `nonbg | (|pixel-bg| sum > 45)`, 7px opening, then take the median left/right edge of row runs wider than 45% of the image. Overlay the measured rects in red on contact sheets before trusting them; panels with an outer decorative ring (h09) need an inset of ~30px.
- Table rows != drawn boxes on most panels: group consecutive rows so every row is covered, reuse only wording already on the slide (incl. notes) and keep [미검증]/[해석] tags; a label that names something absent from the slide (old h05 "실사용 평가") must be replaced.
- One `on()` helper with measured `[x0,y0,x1,y1,px,py]` per box (pictogram left x / top y) handled all 18 panels: thin box → vertically centred, right edge `px-0.018`; tall box → top-hung full width unless it would reach the icon. Panels with a corner bracket (h16) need `dy` and fs 10. Two-line fs 11 pills fit when line 2 ≤ ~15 Hangul in a ~3 in wide pill; trust the LibreOffice render over qa_check's overflow warning.

## Success pattern: section j panel labels (healthcare-fhir-dicom, 2026-11)
- Opening-based measurement (bg from margin strip, colour-distance >60, 15px opening, row runs >40% width) worked on all 24 j panels; only double-outlined panels (j15) and a pale box misread the right edge, so overlay in red and copy x0/x1 from the neighbouring boxes. Search pictograms only in the lower-right of each box (j17 icons were first found at the top).
- Let `on()` throw when label count != box count; no j image needed regeneration. Estimate label width (Hangul 1.0 em, Latin ~0.55, space 0.32) to catch qa_check overflow warnings: j17/j18/j22/j24 labels cleared them by dropping spaces around `·` or swapping in slide-sourced shorter tools/terms.

## Success pattern: section d panel labels (healthcare-fhir-dicom, 2026-11)
- Per-row longest run of `|pixel-bg|>40` (gap-merge 14px, run width 40-93% of the image, consecutive rows = one box) measured all 19 d panels in one pass (pure-python row loop ~2 min: cache boxes to JSON). Outlined cards (d03 thick cream-filled outline, d10/d16/d17 rounded corners) show up as thin top/bottom bands or split boxes: merge them by hand from the printed bands, then overlay red rects before trusting them. Icon search inset must be >= 16px inside the box or the outline band is read as the icon.
- Flow panels (arrows) follow the process order, not the slide table's row order (d03, d08, d16): do not flag them for regeneration; instead name the table's own packages/values in line 2 of each label so every row is still covered, and group consecutive rows when rows > boxes (d01 8 rows -> 6 boxes, d19 7 rows -> 4 boxes).

## Success pattern: regenerating contradicting panels (healthcare-fhir-dicom, 2026-11)
- A panel contradicts its table only when box count/arrow direction/pictogram meaning differ: 12 of 12 candidates (b11 b16 f12 f17 h03 h07 i01 i06 i09 i15 i16 i18) were real; fixed by prompts with the exact box count (N equal boxes, "no connectors" for parallel rows, chevrons only for flows), then re-measure and let `on()` throw on count mismatch.
- If a prompt says "solid saturated flat colour" the model stops producing cream outline-only boxes (which break colour-distance measurement); a re-roll may add faint ghost text in one fill or corner crop marks: re-roll once, then wipe non-background pixels in the margins outside the box bounding box with PIL instead of rerolling again. Sibling panels carry a thin frame anyway.
- `pgrep -f gen_images.py` matches its own shell; use `ps -eo pid,etime,args | grep "[g]en_images"`. gen_images.py processes ids in prompt-file order and skips ids whose raw+final PNG exist.

## Success pattern: 10-author fleet for the 193-slide FHIR/DICOM Korean handbook (healthcare-fhir-dicom, 2026-11-05)
- Pipeline that worked: SPEC.md (binding contract: tag legend, table rules, build rules) + 10 section authors in parallel -> ONE sequential image generator (shared MAI endpoint rate-limits) -> per-section label agents (measure boxes, `on()` throws on count mismatch) -> read-only rubber-ducks (legal for g/h/i, technical for b-f/j, code for d/e) -> one fixer agent per section pair (never two agents on the same section file) -> single regen agent for contradicting panels -> full build + validate + 8 report-only visual inspectors on pre-rendered PNGs (render once yourself; inspectors only view). Total wall time ~6 h, mostly authors.
- Rubber-ducks caught real legal/technical slips authors had marked [문서]: oversimplified 과징금 가중 요건 (§64의2②), wrong sub-clause for the 안전조치 exception (§64-2①9호 단서, not ⑨), 정보통신망법 §48-3 deemed-report clause (breach paths are NOT always cumulative), 의료법 §90 penalty missing in one slide but present in another, 'N items' titles with M table rows (Bundle.type is 10 in R5, search types 9). Cross-section consistency (g vs h vs i vs j) is where most errors hide: have one reviewer read all legal sections together.
- A rubber-duck that reports `Authorization: ******` bugs is seeing tool-output secret masking, not the file: verify with `od -c` before assigning a fix (the f-string was `Bearer {token}`). Reviewers' "premise" dates also need checking (a review claimed §6-2 effective 2026-10-31; the 부칙 says 2025-10-31 with only other clauses delayed).
- A fixer must verify the reviewer's claim on the primary source (law.go.kr) before editing; instruct fixers to touch only their section files and to rebuild+qa_check+render the edited slides themselves.

## Success pattern: reviewer law fixes in the l/a decks (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- law.go.kr full article text: GET `/LSW/lsInfoR.do?lsiSeq=<seq>&efYd=<ef>&chrClsCd=010202&ancYnChk=0` (seq/ef from `/법령/<name>`), strip HTML. Findings: 의료법 §23④ access-log retention is conditional (추가기재·수정), widened to 기재·열람 from 2026-12-10 (법률 제21776호); 시행령 §49②1호 = 매출액 **또는 세입** 1,500억; PIPA §28의2 consent exception is NOT 생명윤리법 IRB/동의 (§15·§16·§36·§37).
- Splitting a scorecard criterion into two neutral-scored criteria and splitting its weight (10 -> 6+4) leaves totals/break-evens unchanged, so no slide numbers or panel images need changes; panels are group-based (4 boxes), only the "기준 7–9" label text changes.
- `qa_check.py` does not inspect tables (graphic frames): render with soffice -> pdftoppm in the project dir and look at tables/callouts yourself. A 9-data-row table breaks SPEC's <=8-row limit; it fit at rowH 0.47 with 2-line cells and a 1-line callout, but a real split needs a new slide id.
- Validate user JSON in CLI samples with key-set equality + `math.isfinite` + bool rejection + duplicate-key `object_pairs_hook`, and put every rejection case in `--selftest`.

## Success pattern: measuring panel boxes under frames/corner brackets (databricks-vs-fabric section e labels, 2026-11)
- A plain "non-background columns > 60% of the box height" test returns x 0.03-0.97 on panels with a drawn frame (e01/e03/e08/e10): the frame lines pass as columns. Instead find box rows from the row profile (non-bg pixels > 45% of width, run >= 30 px), then take the continuous non-bg run around the panel centre on probe rows at 12/20/30% of the box height (the top 60% is icon-free) and the vertical run on probe columns at 30/45% of the width. Do NOT probe lower rows: cream pictogram pixels equal the paper colour and cut the run (e03 x1 0.78).
- Pictogram left edges from a colour-diff scan are polluted by corner brackets (e05/e10 0.55-0.75); read one `ix` per image from the PNG (plug icons reach furthest left) and stop labels at `ix - 0.02`. Detailed scratch scripts: `deck/lb_e_*.py` (deleted after use).

## Success pattern: measuring + labeling section c panels (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- Saturated-fill boxes: mask `|pixel-bg|` sum > 60, MinFilter(15)->MaxFilter(15) to drop icons/specks, per-row longest run (gap-merge 14px, 40-93% width), consecutive rows = box, medians for x0/x1 (numpy+PIL only, ~55 s for 13 panels). Cream outlined boxes with a colored top stripe (c03) come out as stripes only: measure their outline bands by hand and overlay red rects before trusting numbers.
- Rows > boxes (c02, c10: 6 rows -> 5 boxes): group consecutive rows into one label; product x aspect 2x2 grids (c03): name the table's row names in line 2. No regen needed.
- White text on the `amber` pill is ~2.3:1 (fab/moss ~3.2, dbx ~3.7): map caution boxes to the navy `dark` pill instead. `qa_check.py` does not check contrast.

## Success pattern: measuring section d panels (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- Thick-outline boxes (light inner highlight) split row bands: take fg rows from the density in x 0.22-0.30 W (> 0.9), close gaps <= 8 px, pair top/bottom bands <= 40 px for cream outlined boxes (d08, d11), accept only box heights 0.10-0.30 H (rejects frame lines). x0/x1 = median first/last fg x over the middle 30-70% of each box's rows, limited to x 0.06-0.94 W; corner marks still pollute (d11 fixed by hand: x0 0.141, x1 0.859). Check a red-overlay contact sheet before trusting numbers.
- Layout rule that rendered cleanly for all 12 panels: boxes >= 1.0 in tall get a top-hung full-width pill (cut at pictogram x - 0.018 if it would touch the pictogram); thin boxes (d04, d11 ~0.8 in) get a centred pill ending left of the pictogram. 2-line 12pt pill ~0.52 in.
- Tables with more rows than boxes (d02, d03, d05, d06, d07, d09, d10): label from the slide's own wording per box; `on()` throws on count mismatch, no regen needed.

## Success pattern: measuring + labeling section a panels (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- Cream bg + one centred column of saturated boxes: mask `!(lum>195 & sat<70)`, MinFilter(21)->MaxFilter(21) (PIL rank filters take ~2 min for 12 images, run once and cache the JSON), box y-runs from the centre column, x0/x1 as the median over rows at 15-45% of the box height. Measuring x on the box's mid row clipped a08 box 2 (0.725) because the bright pictogram breaks the mask.
- Per-box pill tone: product tone (dbx/fab) only when the label names that product, azure/pal where the box is azure/slate, navy `dark` for violet/amber/green/teal-neutral boxes. Tall boxes (>=1.4 in) top-hung 14pt pill; qa_check's width estimate (box w*72-20 pt, Hangul 1 em) flagged "리전 지원·인증 [미검증]" at 12pt in a 2.1 in pill: shorten the label rather than the font.

## Success pattern: section g panels, pale boxes + pictogram tile (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- Pale-fill boxes (g11, fill |bg| distance ~57) fall under a `>60` mask and one of six boxes vanishes (5 found): print a column profile at `d>25` for the missing y-range and add that box by hand. Every box has a lighter pictogram tile in its lower-right: measure its left edge (`diff vs box fill >70`, search right 45% x lower 70%, columns with >=3 px), take the per-image minimum and end every pill at `tile_x - 0.015`; then a vertically centred navy pill never touches the icon, even in 1.07 in boxes.
- Same-hue pills are invisible (dbx pill on red-orange, fab on teal): all-Databricks (g09) and all-Fabric (g07) panels use the navy `dark` pill. Labels reworded to the table's own terms (dropped "AIM", "DoD IL2", "ISMS-P 체계" that were not on the slides); no panel needed regeneration.

## Success pattern: section h panels, single-column cream boxes (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- Median of the whole image is NOT the background when saturated boxes dominate: take bg from the outer 3% columns, then mask `|px-bg|>90`, Min/MaxFilter(21), row runs > 0.3 W; all 10 panels gave the exact box count first try (no regen). Pictogram left edge: diff from the box fill in the right 45%; read one `ix` per image (per box where the pictogram varies, e.g. textured blue h09) and end pills at `ix-0.02`.
- Label text must come from the slide: h09 "연구·AI 학습"/"DR 연습"/"간격이 RPO를 결정" were not on the slides and were replaced; rows > boxes (h09 5->4) group consecutive rows; flow panels keep process order and name the table's values in line 2. Navy `dark` pills on every saturated box (same-hue product pills vanish).

## Success pattern: section i panels, stacked-column blank boxes (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- For a single column of saturated boxes on cream paper (764x1136, mode P -> `convert("RGB")`), numpy only: `bg = lum>195 & sat<70`, row runs of `fg.mean(axis=1)>0.35` give each box band, then the widest column run (`>0.5`) inside the band gives x0/x1 (chevrons/frames drop out). All 14 panels returned the prompted 4/5 boxes, no regen; draw the rectangles on a contact sheet once to confirm.
- Prompted GEO (x .12-.88) was off per image (real x .075-.925 ... .177-.823, y .055-.95): always measure. Rows > boxes (i02 5->4, i03 7->4, i05 8->4, i06 7->4, i13 5->4): group rows so every table row is named, and use the slide's own tags/numbers ("[미검증]", "$0.63(3×)"); labels like "월 비용×12" or "선불·할인" that the slide never states were replaced. qa_check's overflow warning (i03 "SQL·Auto/Int. VM 포함") cleared by shortening to "서버리스 2종".

## Success pattern: section j panels, white-interior boxes + icon strip (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- A saturation/lum mask misses white boxes with a coloured outline (j07: x read .192 instead of the outer outline .169-.831, box 4 y too short). Use `max|px-paper|>22` against the paper colour (241,233,216) for such panels; the vertical scan at x=.3 then gave all 6 bands. The j07 pictogram is a full-height tile starting at x .724, so every label stops there (`IX` table in `j.js`: per-image pictogram left edge, label right = IX-.015, centred vertically); no regen needed for j01-j10.
