- Replaced label words the slide never shows ("SDP", "DL", "가드레일", "표 데이터 ML", "거버넌스·비용") with the slide's own terms; 4-box j09/j10 labels use fs 13.

## Success pattern: section l panels, mixed filled/outlined boxes (databricks-vs-fabric, 2026-11)
- One numpy-only column scan did all 17 panels: paper colour = most common 8-level-quantised colour, `dist>40` along x=.25 gives y-runs (run >=30px = filled box; thin 2-8px runs are outline pairs -> box = first-top..second-bottom), then a row scan at 30% box height (x .06-.94, so frames drop out) gives x0/x1. Pictogram left edge = min x of `dist(fill)>70` in the lower-right quadrant per box; take the minimum per image (`ICON_X`). Overlay the rects on a contact sheet once to confirm. No regen needed (17 panels all had the prompted counts); l13 has a stray clipboard icon in box 1's upper-left, so its labels start at x .185.
- Labels that mapped the wrong slide item ("순서 = 개방형 먼저" when the slide's 순서 is 비즈니스→…→상업, 개방형 belongs to 방식), invented numbering (①–⑤, "기준 1–2") or invented words ("약속") were replaced with the slide's own row names/weights; 6 table rows on 5 boxes (l03) -> last box names both rows, 9 criteria on 4 boxes (l05) -> row names with weights.

## 2026-11-05 — [SUCCESS PATTERN] Fleet pipeline for a 147-slide comparison deck survives daily reboots (databricks-vs-fabric)

**Pattern:** log PLAN.md (phases, reusable agent briefs, recovery steps) + STATUS.md before any work; keep every stage resumable from files (`gen_images.py` skips existing PNGs, per-section `status/<id>.md`). After a reboot, agents and generators are gone but the 10-min schedule survives; relaunch from PLAN.md §5. Order that worked: authors -> rubber-duck content QA (found 4 blockers: wrong cost model, unequal vCore comparison, law mis-stated as sufficient, unverified claim) -> fixers -> images -> labels -> full build -> 8 visual inspectors + 1 cross-section rubber-duck -> polish.
**Failure route:** an image model can draw one box more than the prompt asks (b05); count boxes from PIL measurement, make `on()` throw on label/box count mismatch. A rubber-duck found a required sample failing on a missing dependency (`pyarrow`) — declare prerequisites in the sample docstring. Don't set text <12pt to fix tight cards (qa_check errors); enlarge the card instead.
Full story: databricks-vs-fabric/STATUS.md.

## 2026-11-05 — [FAILURE ROUTE] `soffice --convert-to pdf` on .docx says "source file could not be loaded"

**Symptom:** Even a trivial python-docx file fails to render; pptx rendering worked fine.
**Root cause:** Only `libreoffice-impress`/`draw` were installed; `libreoffice-writer` was missing, so there is no Writer import filter (the error is not about the file).
**Fix / pattern to reuse:** `sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libreoffice-writer`. Also: single-pass author agents produced ~9 real factual/blocker defects in 88 Q&A items (wrong √10, N-1 latency, over-claimed gradient-vanishing, copied book example) that only independent rubber-duck QA with python3 re-computation caught — always QA numeric Q&A with recomputation, then re-verify the fixes (the re-check caught 1 more blocker).

## 2026-11-09 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FAILURE ROUTES] AFD-in-front-of-image-API latency deck (afd-gptimage)

**Pattern:** the answer is a python model (`model.py` -> `model_out.json`) that `build.js` reads, so every slide number is recomputable; rubber-duck then re-derived them. Facts that mattered: AFD cannot cache POST generation, so only the network path (handshake + response transfer) shrinks and inference is unchanged; AFD Zone 8 = Korea ($0.14/GB egress, $0.16/GB edge->origin, $35/$330 base); Foundry/Azure OpenAI is not a direct Private Link origin (put APIM/App Service between); streaming-through-AFD buffering is unverified -> PoC.
**Failure routes:** (1) a `node_modules` symlink is NOT ignored by `.gitignore`'s `node_modules/` (dirs only) -> use `NODE_PATH` instead. (2) Quoting one range ("0.6~2.0 s") that mixes sizes/scenarios, or labelling two modelled loss cases "하한/상한", overclaims; say "무손실~손실 0.01% 시나리오" and give the 8 MB case separately. (3) Hollow boxes with a thick coloured border defeat the column-scan in `measure_geo.py` (0 boxes): pair saturated top/bottom border runs and measure x along the top border row. (4) White text on `*Fill` tones (amber/clay/moss) is ~2:1; panel labels use the darker base tones. (5) Don't quote a Q&A "unresolved" issue without re-reading it (the 60 s timeout was later not reproducible).

## 2026-05 — pptxgenjs bar chart makes PowerPoint reject the file (LibreOffice/python-pptx still open it)
- Symptom: PPTX "unreadable" in PowerPoint; python-pptx and soffice render fine.
- Root cause: pptxgenjs 2D bar charts emit a phantom third `<c:axId>` in `<c:barChart>` that matches no axis (schema violation). Also avoid ZIP directory entries and keep `[Content_Types].xml` first.
- Fix: in build.js post-process, strip the 3rd axId and rewrite the zip without `.dir` entries (see afd-gptimage/deck/build.js).
- Detect: run `python3 ~/.agents/skills/pptx/scripts/office/validate.py -v <file>` after every build; "renders in LibreOffice" is NOT proof PowerPoint opens it.

## 2026-11 — pptxgenjs decks "unreadable" in PowerPoint though XSD, Open XML SDK, LibreOffice and python-pptx all pass
- Symptom: AFD, Databricks-vs-Fabric and FHIR/DICOM decks rejected by PowerPoint; every automated checker was green (`validate.py` and the .NET Open XML SDK validator both 0 errors, after the chart axId fix).
- Defects found that no schema checker reports: (a) pptxgenjs gives a table `graphicFrame` the same `<p:cNvPr id>` as a neighbouring shape (9-17 slides per deck); (b) the JSZip `loadAsync`+`generateAsync` rewrite in build.js adds ZIP directory entries (`_rels/`, `ppt/`) ahead of `[Content_Types].xml`. The AFD chart's phantom `c:axId` was a third, separate cause.
- Fix: `pptx-tools/pptx_sanitize.py <deck.pptx>` (renumber duplicate ids, drop dir entries, `[Content_Types].xml` first); every `deck/build.js` now calls it last. Run it on any pptxgenjs output before handing a file over.
- Check recipe: a throwaway `dotnet` console app using `DocumentFormat.OpenXml` `OpenXmlValidator` catches the chart error that `validate.py` also catches; it does NOT catch duplicate ids, so scan `p:cNvPr` ids per slide yourself.
- Not provable here: no real PowerPoint on the box. If a deck still fails, ask the user for the exact repair-dialog text and Office build before guessing again.

## pptxgenjs 4.0.1 raw output triggers PowerPoint "repair" even when XSD/Open XML SDK validators pass (2025)
- **Symptom:** every pptxgenjs deck unreadable in desktop PowerPoint; python-pptx, LibreOffice, `validate.py` and the .NET Open XML SDK validator all pass. Older decks only opened because they had been re-saved by PowerPoint.
- **Root cause (known upstream defects, gitbrent/PptxGenJS#1441/#1442/#1444/#1449/#1532):** `<p:sp>` without `<p:txBody>`; `<p:bgPr>` without `<a:effectLst/>`; one ghost `slideMasterN` Override per slide in `[Content_Types].xml` (only slideMaster1 exists); `image/jpg` MIME; notesMaster sharing theme1; duplicate cNvPr ids with tables.
- **Fix:** `pptx-tools/pptx_sanitize.py` (run at end of every `build.js`) now repairs all of these. Run it on any pptxgenjs output.
- **Technique:** when validators are green but PowerPoint complains, search the upstream issue tracker (`gh api search/issues repo:gitbrent/PptxGenJS`) and compare against a PowerPoint-resaved file; real PowerPoint is not available here, so state that honestly.

## 2026-11 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FAILURE ROUTES] Real A/B test of AFD in front of Foundry gpt-image-2.5 (afd-gptimage/realtest)
- **Finding:** a model-only AFD latency estimate was wrong in logic: it ignored the input-image *upload* leg. Measured (Korea Central VM -> eastus2 Foundry, direct vs AFD Standard, paired): AFD cut 8 MB upload 5.2->2.6 s and a 16 MB edit call 27.7->20.9 s (4/4 pairs); generation, JPEG, 3 MB edit and 1536 high-quality showed NO detectable gain (inference jitter +-2 s hides it). New-connection TCP+TLS saves 0.53 s but first byte is ~0.19 s later (cold AFD->origin), so small GETs net 0; with connection reuse 0.23 vs 0.24 s.
- **Technique:** "validate by measuring, not by reading docs" — interleave arms with alternating order, report paired median + bootstrap CI, count failures per arm, and use a no-inference probe (origin rejects with 400 after the body arrives) to isolate network effects for free. Always disclose that the VM was 0.5 ms from the AFD edge (best case for AFD).
- **Failure routes:** (1) 2.5 image deployments are limited to 2 RPM as a sliding 60 s window: pace starts >=33 s apart (start-to-start, not end-to-start) or you get 429s; request quota first (default 2). (2) A new AFD endpoint serves 404 for ~27 min before the route propagates — poll, don't re-create. (3) Foundry account had key auth disabled: use `az account get-access-token --resource https://cognitiveservices.azure.com` as Bearer. (4) Building multi-URL `curl -w` commands in Python is fragile (headers/format apply oddly, 401s); use `http.client` with one persistent connection for keep-alive tests. (5) `az group delete` + `az cognitiveservices account deployment delete` the temp resources when done.

## 2026-11 — Defender family × Foundry agents: agent-level features moved to Agent 365 (LGU+ deck, sections/def.js)
- **Finding (Learn wins over older briefs):** since 2026-07-01 Foundry *agent* inventory/posture/threat protection moved from Defender for Cloud (CSPM / AI services) to Defender XDR + Agent 365 (`defender-xdr/security-for-ai/transition-agent-security-to-agent-365`); Defender for Cloud still bills per Azure resource and is NOT in M365 E7. ME7 = E5 + Copilot + Agent 365 + Entra Suite, so XDR agent security, MDA, MDE P2, MDI and Entra agent controls are "ME7 포함"; Defender Vulnerability Management is a separate add-on; Security Copilot is E5/E7 with phased rollout. XDR agent detection + real-time protection and MDE runtime protection are Preview.
- **Technique:** in `L.table`, a `runs` cell with an empty trailing run renders an extra line (row grows ~0.12in); and the lib's row-height estimate is optimistic for Latin-heavy cells in NanumGothic — place content below a table from the *rendered* image, not only `{bottom}`. A run with `highlight` in a table cell forces a line break after it in LibreOffice (inline "Preview" tag → use bold coloured text); single-line rows render ~0.29in, 2-line ~0.39in, 3-line ~0.5in.

## 2026-11 — Gantt/schedule slide from pptxgenjs shapes + Foundry private-networking facts (LGU+ deck, sections/front.js)
- **Technique (shape Gantt):** x(date) = origin + days × inches/day (0.12 in/day fits 11/10→12/20 in 4.8 in). pptxgenjs has no pattern fill, so "open-ended" regions are hatched with clipped 45° `line` segments (`L.arrow(..., head:"none")`, 0.5pt, ~0.13in pitch); open-ended bars use `homePlate`. Draw order: band fills → hatch → grid → bars → deadline line (so it stays visible). Name 8pt captions `Pill …`/`Node Sub` so `qa_check.py` treats them as exempt from the 9pt floor. Check weekdays first: 2026-12-20 is a **Sunday** (practical deadline Fri 12/18) and 2026-11-10 is a Tuesday.
- **Finding (Learn vs Learn):** Foundry Agent Service private networking how-to allows CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10 for the agent subnet but the networking deep-dive says unsupported — recommend RFC1918 only. Agent subnet: delegated to `Microsoft.App/environments`, portal minimum /27 but deep-dive says /24 for production, one dedicated subnet per Foundry resource, hosted-agent VNet injection only at account creation. Korea Central models are Global Standard / Data Zone Standard (APAC); Regional Standard is essentially only text-embedding-3-large. AI Gateway for MCP in Foundry is Preview (new MCP tools only, APIM v2).

## 2026-11 — Foundry platform slides (LGU+ deck, sections/fdy.js): render workflow traps + RBAC facts
- **Failure routes:** (1) `render.sh` uses `mktemp -d /tmp/...`; where /tmp is off-limits run `soffice.py "-env:UserInstallation=file://$PWD/out/<prof>"` with `TMPDIR` inside the project and delete the profile after. (2) Issuing `view` in the same parallel batch as the render returns "does not exist" or a STALE jpg — always view after the render command has finished, and use a new filename prefix per pass (`p2-`, `p3-`) so an old image is never mistaken for the fix. (3) NanumGothic line height is taller than the `L.node` overflow estimate: nodes with title+sub need h ≥ 0.45 even if no warning fires; confirm in the render.
- **Finding:** Learn `rbac-foundry` (2026-10) — Foundry User/Owner/Account Owner/Project Manager = renamed Azure AI *; new 5th role **Foundry Agent Consumer** (call-only, agent-level scope). Project Manager cannot create projects (matrix) though one sample says it can; publishing needs ≥ Project Manager at resource scope; Azure Contributor cannot publish. Capability hosts need account+project scope, are immutable and default to Microsoft-managed storage (BYO Cosmos/Storage/AI Search = standard setup).
- **Technique (QA pass 1):** U+2011 and NBSP (`"\u00A0· "` between list items) render cleanly in NanumGothic and stop "MAI-/Thinking-1" and line-initial "·" wraps; `qa_check.py` warns on a literal `[미검증]` in a text frame (table cells are not scanned) — put the bracket tag in the table/notes and use plain wording in the caption. Pills inside a node (top-right, centred on the title) read cleaner than pills straddling the border; a bus (`head:"none"` trunk + arrowed ticks) in the gutter between two zones lets one source reach several targets. Sub-lines wrap at ~1.5in/8.5pt: "PTU 예약 · 배치 50% 할인" did not fit a 1.675in card.

## 2026-11 — Managed VNet vs BYO VNet slides (LGU+ deck, sections/net.js)
- **Finding (Learn vs Learn):** `how-to/managed-virtual-network` lists 18 supported regions (Korea Central NOT included) yet also says "all regions where Agent Service custom VNet is supported" (Korea Central = Yes in limits-quotas-regions); managed-network CLI group is Preview but the page never states feature GA/Preview. Deck shows `Preview (CLI)` and keeps the ambiguity in notes as [미검증]. Modes: Allow internet outbound / Allow only approved outbound / Disabled (one-way transitions); FQDN rules auto-create a Microsoft-managed Azure Firewall.
- **Technique:** `L.node` with h<0.34 has no dot and with h 0.34-0.4 the dot is 0.18-0.2in so 2-3 letter icons wrap ("A/G") — use `dot:false` for compact nodes; 2-line subs need h>=0.56 at 8.5pt; `L.table` first-col bold at 1.2in estimates 2 lines (+0.12in/row) — widen col 1 to 1.4 and pass `rowH: 0.27` to fit 8 rows.

## 2026-11 — [SUCCESS PATTERN] Independent fact-check of deck slides 5-21/26-30 (LGU+ deck)
- **Technique:** verify policy slides mechanically — `gh api -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw' repos/Azure/azure-policy/contents/built-in-policies/policyDefinitions/<folder>/<file>` and compare displayName / `parameters.effect.allowedValues` / defaults / `metadata.deprecated`; recounting effects over the 26 active account-level defs reproduced slide 28's legend exactly (Audit16/Deny9/Modify2/DINE7/AINE4/Disabled26) and all spot-checked IDs/names matched. ## 2026-11 — [FAILURE ROUTES] net.js QA pass: diagram connector mapping, isolation-mode naming, START_N off-by-one (LGU+ deck)
- **Failure routes:** (1) Arrows into a grouped "resources" box that don't land on individual nodes read as wrong mappings — align node rows with the source rows and use a head-less bus (`head:"none"` trunk + short arrowed branches) so every dependency has its own arrowhead. (2) Arrows crossing a `L.zone` label or a centered arrow label colliding with it: draw the zone without `label` and place a centered `L.text` between the arrows. (3) `L.node` title wider than w-0.54in wraps and pushes the sub outside the box (e.g. "APIM AI Gateway" in 1.7in) — shorten title, not font.
- **Finding:** managed-network isolation mode is `allow_internet_outbound` / `allow_only_approved_outbound` in the CLI (`az cognitiveservices account managed-network create --managed-network`, Preview group) but PascalCase `AllowInternetOutbound` / `AllowOnlyApprovedOutbound` in Bicep `IsolationMode` / REST `isolationMode`; "Disabled" has no CLI value (no managed network created).
- **Technique:** `node build.js --only <id>` numbers slides START_N+1.. (state.n increments before use) — to get deck slides 5-9 use `START_N=4`.

## 2026-11 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FAILURE ROUTES] 35-slide Korean LGU+ EASM rollout deck from a pinned template with an 11-author fleet (lgu-easm-rollout)
- **Failure routes:** (1) The 6 reference `.pptx` files in `microsoft_foundry/` are IRM-encrypted (CDFV2, `file` says "Composite Document File"); markitdown/python-pptx/unzip all fail and bypassing is out of bounds — check `file *.pptx` FIRST, then source content from Microsoft Learn plus the user's pasted briefs and tell the user. (2) Impeccable's web-UI defaults (and the repo's MAI-image/logo/13.33in conventions) conflict with a "use this template's look" brief: the brief wins — pin the template palette/fonts/10x5.625in canvas and use native shapes only; `impeccable detect` is for web UI and does not apply to pptx. (3) QA agents reading LibreOffice renders report phantom spaces around Latin/Korean runs ("8 개", " .") — render-only autospace artifact, tell authors to ignore it.
- **Success pattern:** shared `lib.js` (template chrome + `table/node/arrow/callout/pill` helpers) + `SPEC.md` (tone semantics, floors, source/notes rules) + `build.js` section loader + `qa_check.py` static checker + `render.sh`; one author per `sections/<id>.js`; then 4 visual + 2 content QA agents (report-only) → one consolidated per-section fix list sent back with `write_agent` → authors fix, rebuild their section and self-verify → full rebuild → second look. Global rules in the fix list ("cut copy, don't shrink fonts"; 8.5pt table / 9pt callout floors; 0.1in clear of the source caption) beat per-slide nitpicks. An author that rewrites its section from scratch removes the file mid-run — `build.js` then prints "(skip <id>: not written yet)" and numbers shift; only trust a full build after every author reports.
- **Second QA pass (fresh agents on the rebuilt renders) paid for itself:** it caught what the per-author self-checks could not — a deck-wide inconsistency (Track pill present on ~half the slides, position varying). Fix = derive it from one source of truth (agenda section→Track map) and send every author the exact `L.pill(...)` call + rule "status pills LEFT of the Track pill, right edge x=9.5". Also catch: arrows converging on one point, labels sitting on connector lines (give them a white-filled pill), callouts <0.1in from the table above, and tables that `L.table` under-estimates in NanumGothic (view the render, don't trust `{bottom}`). Do the full rebuild only after ALL authors report, otherwise a half-written section file silently drops slides.
- **Finding:** Learn conflicts to carry as [미검증] rather than resolve: APIM MCP-server docs show neither Preview nor GA (Foundry's AI-Gateway-for-MCP integration is Preview); Managed VNet region list excludes Korea Central yet says "all regions"; CGNAT range allowed on one page, unsupported on another.

## 2026-11 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FINDINGS] LGU+ deck v2 (13-item change list, 35 → 38 slides, 6-agent fleet) (lgu-easm-rollout)
- **Success pattern (revision round):** treat the user's numbered change list as the work breakdown (no tracker issues needed), re-anchor every derived number from ONE source of truth (Gantt `X(m,d)` + a package-date table), then grep notes for stale dates and slide-number cross-references after slides are inserted — each new slide shifts every "슬라이드 N" in notes (9 → 10 etc.). Always `node build.js --out <v2 path>`; the default output overwrites v1. Per-author sections stay independent, so only the front/back owner rebuilds the whole deck.
- **Finding (customer question "which account is the Agent subnet per?"):** the delegated Agent subnet (`Microsoft.App/environments`) is dedicated to ONE Foundry *resource* (`Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts`), not to a project/subscription/tenant; several projects in that account share it, a second Foundry account needs its own subnet. Hosted agents use the same subnet — no extra subnet or address space, ~1 IP per concurrent session; /27 minimum, /24 recommended.
- **Finding (private MCP hosts):** Learn documents only Azure Container Apps (internal-only ingress, delegated subnet) for a private MCP. Functions/App Service behind a private endpoint with public access disabled returned 403 from the Foundry data proxy (foundry-samples issue); AKS ILB/VM/on-prem are theoretically reachable via the agent subnet but undocumented → label [추정 · PoC 필요]. Do not answer "ACA is the only option" and do not claim others work.
- **Technique:** a Gantt bar label shorter than the bar + its end diamond (≈0.11in) collides when the bar is < ~1.2in (7-day bar at 0.145in/day) — drop the spaces around the dash and use 8.5pt for short bars. Urgency chips need three clearly different hues (green 하 / gold 중 / red 상); a pale-yellow 중 next to a pink 약 reads as the same colour. Background fleet agents are not resumable after the parent context is compacted — keep their outputs on disk (section files) and rebuild from the files.
- **Finding (PE / MCP subnet CIDR, customer Q after v2):** Learn gives NO required size for the Foundry private-endpoint subnet — only the sample 192.168.1.0/24; real need = 1 IP per PE (+Cosmos DB 1 global + 1 per region) + 5 Azure-reserved, smallest Azure subnet is /29. The MCP subnet is a Container Apps environment subnet: workload-profiles env min /27 (supports UDR → needed for the Firewall 0.0.0.0/0 design), consumption-only env min /23 and no UDR; ACA table: /27=18 usable IPs, /26=50, /24=242, /23=498 (14 infra incl. 5 reserved; 1 IP per node on dedicated profile, 1 per 10 replicas on consumption). Deck slides only carried the template-19 sample /24s in notes — state "required minimum vs sample vs proposal" separately when answering sizing questions.
- **Finding (slide 12 "확인 필요": can Foundry Project Manager create projects?):** Learn `concepts/rbac-foundry` contradicts itself — permission matrix says Create Foundry projects = Account Owner/Owner ✔, Project Manager ✘, but the sample enterprise mapping (IT admin / Team lead rows) and the "Partial access isolation" appendix say Project Manager creates projects. Tie-breaker found later: `concepts/administrator-guide` (Elevated-role tasks) lists "Create a Foundry project" min role = Contributor, Foundry Account Owner or Foundry Owner (no Project Manager) and its quick reference gives Project Manager only "publish agents + conditional Foundry User assignment". Evidence favours PM ✘ ([추정], not product-team confirmed) → for RBAC conflicts check administrator-guide before the persona samples; deck slide 12/13 notes still cite only the 2-way conflict.
- **Finding (APIM subnet, customer Q "PE + VNet integration이면 APIM subnet 불필요?"):** inbound Private Endpoint (classic + Standard v2/Premium v2) only needs an IP in the PE subnet (that subnet can't be delegated) — no APIM subnet. Outbound VNet integration (Standard v2 / Premium v2 only) DOES need a dedicated subnet used by one APIM instance only: min /27, recommended /24, NSG mandatory (outbound AzureKeyVault 443), delegation `Microsoft.Web/serverFarms` (Standard v2) or `Microsoft.ApiManagement/service` (Premium v2); inbound NSG rules are not enforced under integration. So the "required subnets" strip (Agent / PE / MCP) is incomplete whenever the AI Gateway must reach a private MCP — add the APIM integration subnet as a 4th, conditional one.

## 2026-11 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FAILURE ROUTES] Fixing a customer-edited copy of the deck (LGES_EASM_Rollout_Plan_KO_v2.pptx)
- **Failure route (root cause of "LG엔솔는/가"):** the LGES copy was made by bulk-replacing "LGU+" → "LG엔솔"; Korean particles are chosen by the last syllable's batchim, so `LGU+는/가/를` becomes wrong (`엔솔` ends in ㄹ → use 은/이/을). After any customer-name substitution, grep paragraph-joined text (runs split the particle: `<a:t>엔솔</a:t>` then `<a:t>는 …</a:t>`) for `엔솔[는가를]`, in slides AND notes.
- **Technique (edit a PowerPoint-modified pptx in place — do NOT rebuild from `deck/sections`):** `unpack.py` → edit `ppt/slides|notesSlides/*.xml` with the edit tool (change only `<a:t>` text so run formatting survives) → `pack.py <dir> out.pptx --original <backup>` → `validate.py -v` → `render.sh` and look. `pack.py` auto-adds `xml:space="preserve"` to many `<a:t>` (harmless, ~250 repairs). Edit `docProps/core.xml` `<dc:title>` for the document-properties title.
- **Technique:** a count change must be swept through title, callout, speaker notes AND the notes' per-item list (notes ①–⑦ had no entry for the table's 8th row). Callout boxes sized for one sentence line + one legend line overflow when the sentence gains ~12 chars — shorten ("…에 접수해야 12/20 준수 가능.") and re-render; resizing the group is not worth it.
- **Finding:** a Private Endpoint subnet must NOT be delegated (error `PrivateEndpointCreationNotAllowedAsSubnetIsDelegated`), unlike the Agent subnet and the ACA MCP subnet (`Microsoft.App/environments`); the customer's "PE … 위임 전용" wording was wrong.
- **Finding:** a Windows NTFS alternate data stream (`<file>.pptx:sec.endpointdlp`, Purview Endpoint DLP label) can get committed as a normal file with a colon in its name — delete it; consider `*:sec.endpointdlp` in `.gitignore`. The sensitivity label also lives in the pptx at `docMetadata/LabelInfo.xml` (leave it).
- **Decision from the user:** "VNet"/"Vnet" is intentional capitalisation, not a typo; slide-10 callout overflow in the customer copy was explicitly ignored.

## 2026-11 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FINDINGS + FAILURE ROUTES] 23-slide Agent 365 Azure Policy/settings appendix deck, 6-author fleet (lgu-easm-rollout, `--deck a365`)
- **Finding (the premise was wrong):** Agent 365 has NO dedicated Azure Policy definitions — it is a Microsoft 365 tenant service, not an ARM resource. `Azure/azure-policy` HEAD `f096d8d` (release 3.2026.1009.2): code search for `agent365`/`a365` = 0 hits. `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/a365LoggingEnabled` exists only as a Modifiable alias (API 2026-03-15-preview, default true); no built-in uses it, so it appears only as an "예시·제안" custom policy. Frame such requests as 3 layers — Azure Policy on the dependent/hosting Azure resources, Agent 365 native settings (policy templates, registry, tools/MCP), Entra/Purview/Defender — and say so on slide 2 instead of inventing policy names. Learn pages disagree with each other (policy-template 12 vs agent-actions 13 defaults; Frontier eligibility; whether an Azure Bot is needed) → carry as [미검증], ledger in `deck/notes/a365_a6_unverified.md`.
- **Technique (build a second deck from the same generator):** `node build.js --deck a365` (sections a1..a6, `DECK_CUSTOMER` env var for the customer name, `setFooter` in `lib.js`); per-section `START_N=<first page − 1> node build.js --deck a365 --only aN`. Authors keep to their own section files, so only the final assembler rebuilds everything. Output is the standalone attachment `LGES_EASM_Rollout_Plan_Appendix_A_Agent365_KO_v1.pptx`.
- **Technique (mechanical GUID fact-check):** sparse-clone `Azure/azure-policy`, index `built-in-policies/policyDefinitions/**/*.json` by `name`, compare with GUIDs extracted from slide text AND notes (also check `policyType`/deprecated flag, displayName, default effect). python-pptx extraction MUST walk tables and group shapes — a first pass over `shape.has_text_frame` only gave false "missing" results. Non-policy GUIDs (role-definition and app IDs) are expected leftovers.
- **Success pattern (fleet):** authors in parallel → trial assemble + qa_check/XSD → fresh-eyes visual QA agents (read-only, 3 × ~7 slides) → per-author fix lists with global decisions stated up front (as-of date, cross-reference wording, term spelling, Track definitions, badge grammar) → rebuild → a SECOND fresh QA round on a new render (it still found ~12 MED, mostly 0.03–0.06in gaps, mixed table-header wording and notation drift). Idle author agents stay addressable by their UUID (`list_agents`), not by name — `write_agent` with the description name fails.
- **Failure route:** authors sometimes edit files with a Python one-liner despite the "create/edit tools only" rule; verify the output rather than assume. `L.bullets` with `[lead, text]` items renders two bullets per item (use a single-paragraph card); the lib's table-height estimate is optimistic for Korean text (~0.40in per 2-line row at 9pt) — verify from the render.
- **Process note:** `sunbigfly/pptx-agent-skills` does not exist; `sunbigfly/ppt-agent-skills` was installed as `~/.agents/skills/ppt-agent` (symlinked into `~/.copilot/skills`). It brings its own HTML→SVG→PPTX pipeline and a broad trigger, so it was NOT used for the template-bound appendix.
- **Finding (customer Q on main-deck slide 27 "Defender for Endpoint + Vulnerability Mgmt: ME7 일부 포함 (취약점 관리는 별도)"):** the product is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management (MDVM). MDE P2 (so M365 E5 → ME7, [추정] per contract) already includes the CORE set (device discovery/inventory, vulnerability + configuration assessment, risk-based prioritisation, remediation tracking, software inventory/usage); only the PREMIUM set is separate — MDVM Add-on (needs MDE P2) or MDVM Standalone (any EDR), and Defender for Servers P2 for servers. Premium = security baselines (CIS/STIG, GPO-only, English locale, PowerShell Constrained Language Mode off), block/warn vulnerable apps (file IOCs via Defender AV active mode + cloud protection + "Allow or block file"; enforced in minutes, up to 3 h), browser-extension inventory (Windows; Edge/Chrome/Firefox; permission risk), certificate inventory (expiry ≤60 d, key <2048, SHA-1/MD5, self-signed), network-share recommendations (4 rules), hardware/firmware inventory (weaknesses only from HP/Dell/Lenovo advisories, processors+BIOS). Windows authenticated scan is deprecated. So "취약점 관리는 별도" over-states it — say "핵심 포함 · 프리미엄(Add-on) 별도". Learn gives NO price; the ~$2/user add-on and ~$3 standalone figures seen online are third-party blog numbers → keep as [미검증], never put them on a slide. Technique: Learn pages carry ~3 KB of front matter, so `web_fetch` with `start_index≈3300` to reach the body.
- **Decision + technique (MDVM slides → appendix, never the customer file):** the user ruled that `LGES_EASM_Rollout_Plan_KO_v2.pptx` is delivered to the customer and must stay byte-intact — any follow-up from a Q&A ("slide 27 over-states it") goes into the appendix deck, not into the delivered file; verify with `git status` / mtime. MDVM is `sections/a7.js` (3 slides: core vs premium zones, 6-row premium table, rollout steps + price-check), hooked from the END of the a5 Defender block via `require("./a7")(pptx, state, L)` so it lands before the control matrix; the deck is now 26 slides (MDVM = p.19–21, matrix p.22, runbook p.23–25, Q&A p.26). Page references to p.5–18 stay valid because the insertion is after p.18; the runbook cites section names, not page numbers. `build.js` now accepts `--only <id>` for helper sections outside `DECKS.a365.order` (a7 alone needs `START_N=18`); before this fix `--only a7` silently produced an empty deck. The table in a7 slide 2 needs `rowH 0.44` (the lib's 0.3 estimate leaves the table overlapping the callout below it).

Details and URLs: `lgu-easm-rollout/deck/notes/trend_f5_notes.md`.

## 2026-11 — [TECHNIQUE + FINDINGS] Researching Hermes Agent for the AI-agent-trends deck (`trend_f3`)
- **Technique:** pull docs/source with `gh api repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/contents/website/docs/... --jq .content | base64 -d` into a scratch dir inside the repo, then `grep` exact config keys in `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` + `cli-config.yaml.example` before putting them on a slide (docs prose and defaults sometimes differ). ## 2026-11 — [TECHNIQUE + FINDINGS] Token-saving slides (`trend_k2`: prompt caching, compaction, progressive disclosure)
- **Technique:** most vendor docs return clean markdown when you append `.md` (Claude/Anthropic, Claude Code, OpenAI) — `curl -sL <url>.md` then `grep`; Gemini explicit caching needs `?generate-content=true`; repo claims via `gh api repos/<o>/<r> --jq .description`. Azure OpenAI Learn gives **no** cache read/write multipliers — get them from the Retail Prices API (`prices.azure.com/api/retail/prices?$filter=contains(skuName,'5.6')`, cached-input and write meters) and label them as such.
- **Finding:** Anthropic caching is opt-in (`cache_control`), OpenAI/Azure/Gemini implicit by default; GPT-5.6+ adds write fees (30m 1.25×, 12h 2.5×) so a busted prefix costs MORE than no cache (+24% in a 30-turn model). No vendor publishes a compaction saving %, and the Gemini implicit-cache TTL is undocumented — say so on the slide instead of inventing numbers.
- **Failure route (build):** `L.table` renders 9.5pt rows ≈0.05in taller than at 9pt and 3-line cells ≈0.55in; make every cell ≤2 lines (widen the column, shorten text) before shrinking fonts; read `t.bottom` from `L.table` to place the block under it. `qa_check` warns on `[추정]/[미검증]` on the slide face — keep evidence tags in the speaker notes. Text across segmented diagram bars gets cut by the gaps — use one continuous bar and put segment names in a header row.

## 2026-11 — [TECHNIQUE + FINDINGS + FAILURE ROUTES] Synthetic PoC data kit + Fabric IQ ontology constraints (`fabric-palantir-poc/samples/`)
- **Technique:** stdlib-only deterministic generator (`random.Random(seed)`, LF/UTF-8, gz with `mtime=0`) + one `ontology_spec.json` as single source for validate.py, build_docs.py (data dictionary + generated md block) and the notebooks → spec/data/docs cannot drift. Notebooks can be run locally without Fabric: venv with `pyspark==3.5.3 delta-spark==3.3.0`, `enableHiveSupport()` + Derby `spark.hadoop.javax.jdo.option.ConnectionURL` under a scratch dir (otherwise tables vanish between the 01 and 02 processes), and `TMPDIR` / `_JAVA_OPTIONS=-Djava.io.tmpdir=` / `SPARK_LOCAL_DIRS` / `-Dderby.system.home` all pointed into a gitignored dir (Spark writes to /tmp by default).
- **Finding (Fabric IQ binding, fabric-docs `docs/iq/ontology/`):** entity key must be string/integer; supported types = integer, boolean, datetime, double, string — **DECIMAL → null in Graph**; managed lakehouse tables only (renaming a bound table breaks it); a column name containing space or `, ; { } ( ) \n \t =` auto-enables Delta column mapping, which is unsupported; relationship names must be unique; entities with several backing tables are not graph-eligible (whether a secondary time-series binding counts is NOT stated → keep as estimate). Old experience (retires 2027-01-31) required property names unique across entity types + 1–26 chars; the new glossary allows same name only with same type — don't mix the two.
- **Finding (Palantir):** time-series sync datasets are long format (`series_id`, `timestamp`, `value`), so a wide per-machine telemetry table needs an unpivot (`gen_data.py --foundry` does it); FK links are 1:1/1:N, N:M needs a join dataset.
- **Failure route:** for a rule demo to have a clear signal, weight inspection lots / lateness toward a few "bad" suppliers instead of uniform sampling; rule tie-order (SUP-020 vs SUP-028, equal counts) must be fixed in the expected value or validate.py flaps. A "late-arriving" demo needs the late rows removed from the base file AND a consecutive-run query that breaks on missing minutes (minute − row_number islands), otherwise R1 gives the same answer before and after.

## 2026-11-17 — [TECHNIQUE + FAILURE ROUTES] Placing pill labels on generated panel images (label tuner h/i/j, `fabric-palantir-poc/deck/labels/`)
- **Technique:** measure, don't eyeball — threshold the PNG (PIL/numpy), take connected components for box/icon rects, convert pill pixel boxes to fractions with a small script, and flag overlaps against "keep-out" rects (icons, arrow origins/heads) before `build.js`. "Edge-straddling tabs" (pill centre on a box's top/bottom edge, or hung just below with `ay:"t"`) never cover icons and read as the box's title. A pill is ≈46 px tall (1 line) / 77 px (2 lines) on a 764×1136 panel; width ≈ (text em-width + 0.2 in) × 1.07 × 186 px/in, so "Microsoft 문서" ≈ 243 px — shorten text rather than overlap neighbours.
- **Failure route:** generated images often contradict the slide (wrong pip counts in h_04, heat-map icons vs ratings in j_02, 2 decision nodes vs 3 questions in j_03, extra Fabric rows in i_04) — label tiers/axes or cover the misleading element with a pill instead of labelling individual items; don't invent content. Cost-section labels may only use numbers that appear on the slide. `render.sh` always writes `s-N.jpg`, so copy to unique names before the next render (the image viewer caches by path).

Apply order: nginx first, ALB health-check path last. Pitfall: `kill 0` in a shell `trap` kills the whole process group — track `$API_PID` and kill that only.
- **Gotcha:** DG box text wraps at ~1.4in; panel canvas is 4.1 × 6.1in and notes outside it fail strict mode. A user's "Azure Queue service" in an AWS context was read as a typo for SQS — state such assumptions in the final report.
- **Pattern (visual-QA fix wave):** after wave 2, run 4 fresh-eyes reviewers per slide range, merge findings into one `.scratch_fix/COMMON.md` brief, then fix with disjoint section ownership (6 agents) and rebuild once. Reject a reviewer claim when the arithmetic checks out (a "2,275 transposition" and "2,492" were both correct); decide totals from `CANONICAL.md`, not from slide text.
- **Gotcha (DG `bars`):** the auto-legend uses pale tints, not the solid bar fills, so a legend and its bars look unrelated; make the series non-solid or label the bars directly. **Dependabot:** enabling alerts lists existing vulnerabilities but only notifies for newly disclosed ones; do not promise a notification for the backlog.
- **Gotcha (pptxgenjs notes):** an unescaped `""` inside a double-quoted JS `notes:` string is a syntax error that stops the whole build; reword or escape. A bar label of "무료" next to a priced item (+USD 25.7) drew a QA finding: say "설정 무료 · 저장비 별도".

## 2026-11-20 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FAILURE ROUTES] Bilingual three.js organ model with a surgical-incision intro (`anatomy/`)
- **Pattern:** one standalone HTML built by `node build.mjs` (esbuild bundle + three.js + Nanum fonts subset with `pyftsubset` and inlined as woff). Expose `window.__anatomy` (state, seek helpers, `screenPos`) so Playwright can drive and assert a WebGL scene; test real mouse drag with those screen positions. Incision = one transparent DoubleSide `ShaderMaterial` shell: `discard` a slit then a widening superellipse window on front faces only, paint the wound edge in the shader, paint `!gl_FrontFacing` as the cavity wall, and set `depthWrite` only while the skin is opaque.
- **Failure route:** hand-lofted tube geometry with inward triangle winding renders the far wall under FrontSide and black under MeshToon+BackSide; fix the index order, do not flip the material. A BackSide stipple hull on a ghost body makes hatching — use a fresnel rim. Fading the skin to alpha at the waist exposed an organ nub; fade to the page colour instead (and not for back faces, or a white patch shows inside the window).
- **Failure route:** food/tracer meshes inside opaque tubes were invisible although their positions were right — draw tracers with `depthTest=false` and a high `renderOrder`. Check `__anatomy.bolus()` before suspecting the animation.
- **Gotcha:** headless swiftshader runs a few fps and the sim `dt` is capped, so lerps need 2–3 s waits (or seek APIs) and play-through tests must poll state. Close the previous Playwright page before opening a second one or `goto` times out. A layout switched on `w/h < 1.05` makes a ~square stage use the portrait shelf. Meal mode auto-plays, so a test that clicks Play first pauses it. Looking down at ~41° foreshortens the torso, so tray rows and camera extents tuned for a level camera clip at the bottom.

## 2026-11-20 — [FAILURE ROUTE + SUCCESS PATTERN] PowerPoint "recover" prompt although every validator is green (`pptx-tools/pptx_sanitize.py`, `pptx-tools/pptx_audit.py`)
- **Symptom:** bonupai v1/v2 (pptxgenjs 4.0.1, with speaker notes) open in PowerPoint with a repair dialog; zip/XSD/Open XML SDK 3.0.2 (0 errors)/`validate.py`/LibreOffice/python-pptx all pass. v1 and v2 are structurally identical, so the cause is in the pipeline, not slide content.
- **Most likely cause (best evidence, not provable without PowerPoint):** gitbrent/PptxGenJS#1443 (fix PR #1458). Mac PowerPoint drops the notesMaster's six hdr/dt/sldImg/body/ftr/sldNum placeholders and then prompts. Proof PowerPoint itself writes the stripped form: Mac-saved decks (`microsoft_foundry/Entra-ID-tempates.pptx`) have a 3.6 KB notesMaster whose spTree is only the root group; Windows-saved decks keep the six placeholders. Second deviation: our sanitizer's blanket `add_txbody` put an empty `<p:txBody>` inside each notes-page `sldImg` placeholder, which PowerPoint never writes (raw pptxgenjs does not either).
- **Fix (v2.1):** `pptx_sanitize.py` now empties the notesMaster spTree (bg/clrMap/notesStyle kept), skips txBody on `sldImg`, and sets `notesSz` to 6858000x9144000. Slide XML is byte-identical and extracted text+notes are identical to v2; the sanitizer is idempotent.
- **Pattern:** compare against a *real PowerPoint-saved* file, not just validators: `Application`+`revisionInfo.xml`/`thumbnail.jpeg` in docProps mark one; diff the part you suspect (here notesMaster). Run `pptx_audit.py` (strict package audit) next to the Open XML SDK validator; neither proves PowerPoint accepts the file.
- **If it still prompts:** ask the user for the exact dialog text, Office build and Mac vs Windows before guessing again. Last-resort fallback is a build without notes (drop notesMaster + notesSlides), which loses the speaker notes this deck relies on.
- **Gotcha:** a "PowerPoint-looking" `docProps/app.xml` (`Application=Microsoft Office PowerPoint`, large `Words`) is also what pptxgenjs/python-pptx templates write, so it does not prove a file was saved by PowerPoint (`MAI_Decision_1_Guide_KO.pptx` was raw).

## 2026-11-20 — [FAILURE ROUTE] "The incision button does nothing" on a slow GPU (`anatomy/src/main.js`)
- **Symptom:** user reports the button is dead; clicks, taps, keyboard and reduced-motion all worked in headless Chromium at several viewports, so it was not an event bug.
- **Likely cause:** software or weak GPUs render this scene at ~1 fps and the sim `dt` is capped at 0.1 s, so a 6 s cut took about a minute, the CTA vanished at once and nothing told the user it had started. Unconfirmed on the user's machine.
- **Fix pattern:** drive one-shot intro animations by the wall clock, give instant feedback (status text, focus, Skip button), lower render resolution when frames are slow, show a bilingual message for no-WebGL, context loss and repeated render errors, and keep the rAF loop alive with try/catch.
- **Gotcha:** adding a strict CSP (`script-src 'sha256-…'`) breaks Playwright `wait_for_function("string")` (uses eval) and makes `until()` helpers silently return False, which looked like 4–5 animation regressions. Use `bypass_csp=True` and keep one CSP-enforced page that asserts no violations. Check console/`pageerror` before suspecting timing.
- **If it persists:** ask for browser, OS and whether hardware acceleration is on.

## 2026-11-21 — [SUCCESS PATTERN + FAILURE ROUTES] Two bilingual isometric-SVG models built in parallel: car factory and shipyard (`auto-factory/`, `shipyard/`)
- **Pattern:** the `anatomy` skill's isometric SVG kit, one standalone HTML per model (`node build.mjs`), Nanum fonts inlined, pure `stateAt(u)` model driving the picture and the readout, and a `window.__factory` / `window.__shipyard` hook (`seek`, `select`, `hold(true)` + `tick(ms)`) so Playwright can render deterministic frames. Two builder agents ran in parallel with disjoint folders; each got a security review and a rubber-duck review, and the findings went back to the same builder (`write_agent`) so it kept its context. Suites: factory 171 checks, shipyard 163.
- **Pattern (CSP):** hash the assembled script text (`script-src 'sha256-…'`); the script placeholder must be exactly `<script>/*__SCRIPT__*/</script>` on one line or the hash silently mismatches. Run tests with `bypass_csp=True`, keep one real-CSP page, add a tampered-script test.
- **Pattern (tests):** mutate the built page to prove each new test can fail (reviewers found vacuous checks in both suites). Headless software GL gives a real SVG frame only every 3–4 s, so use hold/tick/seek, not sleeps. Wait for a fingerprint to be stable across two frames before asserting "paused is byte-identical" (the camera ease tail is exponential; one run failed by a single character).
- **Failure routes (rubber-duck found these in both):** Pause must freeze everything, so effects need their own clock and in-flight seeks must end; a motion-preference change mid-seek must leave the stage consistent; do not skip UI updates (readouts, chips) when the figure is offscreen, only the SVG redraw; restore focus after a click rebuilds the focused element; the rAF timestamp lies across stalls, use `performance.now()`; do not capture global keys while a control has focus.
- **Gotchas:** rpm ∝ ∛power, so wait for ~1e-6, not 0.002, before asserting stillness. Paint moving parts in fixed slots (back/work/front/fx). A lathe solid costs ~4.7 ms per rebuild vs ~0.2 ms for a prism, so use prisms for per-frame parts. A horizontal scroll strip in a grid item needs `minmax(0,1fr)` or the phone layout widens to 663 px. `[hidden]` needs `!important`. Camera framing from a layer's bounding box can be wrong (a "house" layer included the lifeboat and anchor). Subset fonts hold only the glyphs used, so new Korean text needs a rebuild.
- **Limits:** only headless Chrome on software GL was tested. `auto-factory/kit` is a gitignored symlink to the skill's kit, so a fresh clone needs it recreated to rebuild (the built HTML needs nothing); `shipyard/vendor/` holds a copy.
